damage-healing.stun_damage: Weapons set to stun roll damage normally; any result worse than Stunned becomes unconscious for 2D minutes. All character-scale blasters can be set for stun unless stated otherwise. Changing the setting is an action.

damage_options.severe_injuries: Optional: a character who would kill may instead cause a serious permanent injury; the target is also Wounded, Wounded twice or Incapacitated (gamemaster's choice). Not necessarily evil.
damage_options.massive_damage: Optional: two Wound levels in one round apply the greatest level's modifiers and the character can only defend or run for the next two rounds; each of those rounds an Easy stamina or willpower roll (as an action) may shake it off.

miscellaneous_damage.verified_against: PDF page 104 (the text export misaligns this table)
miscellaneous_damage.rule: Generally no attack roll needed; damage is per round of close contact, except falling. The gamemaster decides what protection armor gives.

natural.rule: Rest the required time, then roll full Strength on the chart for the current Wound level. Working, exercising or adventuring: -1D to the roll. Doing virtually nothing for twice the time: +1D.

medpac.success: Heals one level: stunned and wounded fully healed; unconscious revived; wounded twice -> wounded; incapacitated -> wounded twice; mortally wounded -> incapacitated.
medpac.failure: No change; if the roll misses by more than 10, no more medpacs can be used on that character for a standard day (24 hours).
medpac.multiple_uses: Each additional use within a day raises the difficulty one level.
medpac.consumed: A medpac is expended when used.
medpac.self_use: -1D extra penalty on top of other penalties (wound penalties included).

bacta_tank.requirement: (A) medicine; Very Easy roll regardless of wound level, after which healing is a matter of time. Without (A) medicine: Heroic first aid or Technical roll; failure worsens the injury two levels (wounded -> incapacitated, wounded twice -> mortally wounded, incapacitated or mortally wounded -> killed).

surgery.requirement: (A) medicine, a surgery kit and a medical facility; only when the gamemaster deems it required or no bacta tank is available.
surgery.difficulty: Easy base, raised for complexity and field conditions.

illness_and_poison.status: Optional gamemaster-facing systems: Phase 2. Source: pages 103-105 of raw-data/06-combat-injuries.txt. The illness chart (mild to extreme, damage per interval) and the six result tables by wound level are not distilled yet.
illness_and_poison.illness_note: Armor bonuses do not apply to Strength rolls to resist damage from contaminated water. Counteracting an illness: Difficult (A) medicine or Very Difficult first aid, one attempt per day.

die-code-simplification.description: Bonus numbers to replace rolling many dice. 'fast': roll 5 dice (incl. Wild Die), add the die code's pips and the five_dice_bonus. 'faster': roll only the Wild Die, add pips and the wild_die_bonus. Character Point dice are rolled separately; with a Force Point, double the original die code before looking up the bonus.

difficulty-numbers.rule: Roll equal to or higher than the difficulty number to succeed. In an opposed roll the higher roll wins; ties go to the character who initiated the action.
difficulty-numbers.heroic_steps: Heroic +10 = 40-49, Heroic +20 = 50-59, and so on; numbers can reach 100 or more.
difficulty-numbers.random_difficulty_notes: Optional rule: roll the listed dice (including the wild die) to set the number instead of choosing it.

availability_codes.meaning: Readily available throughout the known galaxy.
Normally available only in large cities and space ports, or on the item’s planet of origin.
Specialized item, normally only available on the item’s planet of origin.
Rare item, difficult to obtain anywhere.

restriction_codes.meaning: Fee or permit often required for purchase.
Restricted on most planets; normally may not be sold without a license.
Illegal on most planets; possession and use generally violates Imperial, Republic or local laws except for authorized individuals.

licenses.rule: The fee is a percentage of the object’s base cost, bought in addition to the object. Then roll bureaucracy or a Knowledge skill; success grants the license after the time shown; failure costs the time and the fee, and you may retry. Bribing an official uses persuasion; a false or stolen identity uses forgery; failing either by 5 or more alerts the authorities. All applications leave a record in public files.

trade.black_market: Most restricted items can be found on the black market for enough effort and money.
trade.selling_items: A merchant generally buys used equipment at half its listed price (commodities excluded).
trade.prices: Listed costs are averages for typical equipment; local tariffs, availability and quality change them at the gamemaster’s discretion.

general_goods.unit_note: Cost in credits per unit shown.

replacement_prosthetics.effect: Duplicates the natural part; no special abilities. A Difficult Perception roll tells it from an organic one.

enhancements.rule: Increase one attribute by a number of pips or dice; every skill under it that is already above the attribute rises equally. Cost for the attribute and for each such skill: base cost x pip increase x starting die code (ignoring pips). The operation must include the attribute and all those skills. Each full die of increase counts as three pips.
enhancements.example: Strength 3D+1 to 5D+1 on a cybernetic hand (base 1,000): 1,000 x 6 pips x 3 = 18,000 credits.
enhancements.replacement_counts_as: half an enhancement (rounded down) for Dark Side Points
enhancements.optional_force_user_penalty: Each prosthetic gives one cyber point; cyber points reduce all Force skills by 2 pips each for enhancements and 1 pip each for replacements.
enhancements.social_cost: Obvious cybernetics meet fear, suspicion and hatred; cybernetics are not meant as a shopping list for player characters.

meaning.control: Control over the Jedi's own body and internal Force.
meaning.sense: Feeling the Force in other things beyond one's own body: danger, information, the bonds between living things.
meaning.alter: Changing the distribution and nature of the Force: moving objects, helping others control their Force, manipulating the Force in other bodies, changing perceptions.

learn_first_time.requirements: A teacher with at least 3D in that skill, higher than the student's skill; only Force-sensitive characters.
learn_first_time.cost: 10 Character Points and one week of intensive study (one day less per extra Character Point, minimum one day).
learn_first_time.result: The skill starts at 1D and the character is taught one power pertaining to it.
learn_first_time.usual_order: Control first (some teachers start with sense), alter last.

improve.cost_per_pip: the number before the 'D' in the current die code; double without a teacher
improve.training: 1 day per Character Point with a teacher; 2 days per Character Point without; 1 day cut per additional Character Point, minimum one day
improve.new_power: Each pip improved lets the teacher choose a new power that uses the improved skill (a control improvement cannot teach an alter-only power).

teaching.pupils: Need a Force skill of at least 3D to teach it and can only teach powers they know. By tradition a student does not take pupils. Teaching someone with Dark Side Points gives the teacher a Dark Side Point. A Jedi is responsible for a pupil who turns to the dark side.
teaching.other_sources: A Holocron, datatape or book may or may not count as a teacher, at the gamemaster's discretion.

rules: A power must be taught before it can be used.
Learning a Force skill for the first time teaches one power for that skill.
Each pip of improvement in a Force skill allows one new power.
A power can be taught without improving a skill for 5 Character Points.
A power that uses two skills counts as two powers when being taught; three skills count as three.
All Required Powers must already be known.

using_powers.skill_rolls: Each Force skill a power uses is a separate action. Roll them in consecutive rounds at no penalty, or all in one round with the normal multiple-action penalty (two skills: -1D each).
using_powers.difficulty: Each power lists a difficulty per skill; the gamemaster may add modifiers. The target may roll control or Perception to resist when the entry says so.
using_powers.stretching_powers: The gamemaster may let players stretch a power to nearby effects: a modest extension raises difficulty one or two levels, the outermost limits may need Heroic +50 or more.
using_powers.keeping_up: Some powers may be kept 'up' (announce when activating): no new rolls each round, but the Jedi loses dice as if taking actions (-1D per Force skill the power uses, e.g. lightsaber combat -2D). Stunned, wounded or worse drops all 'up' powers. If the entry does not say it can be kept up, it ends at the end of the round.
using_powers.warning: Some powers are inherently evil and give a Dark Side Point every use; any power used for evil also does.
using_powers.time_to_use: If no Time to Use is listed the power takes effect in one round.

relationship_modifier.verified_against: PDF page 155 (the text export misaligns the values)

rows.user_and_target: Never met, but known by reputation
Complete strangers, not of the same species

proximity_modifier.verified_against: PDF page 155 and the regenerated text (all eight rows)

rows.user_and_target: In line of sight but not touching
Not in line of sight, 1-100 meters away
Same planet, more than 1,000 km away
Same system, not the same planet
Not in the same star system

dark_side.bonus_to_force_skills: A character with Dark Side Points adds +1D per Dark Side Point to Force skill rolls (3 points = +3D). A Jedi may refuse the bonus, but then all Force power difficulties rise by at least one level. A character who has gone over to the dark side no longer gets the bonus.

ways_to_gain_points.rule: Knowingly and willfully breaking the Jedi Code, including unjustified violence and violence fueled by hate or anger; committing or bringing about evil; using 'dark side' powers (Inflict Pain, Telekinetic Kill, Force Lightning...); using a Force Point for evil. Guideline: an act that makes you say 'That's cold!' is unjustifiable.
'Evil by association': standing idly by while evil is committed or passing on an obvious chance to bring justice gives a point.

Gain a Force Point (spent that round) and a Dark Side Point, successful or not. Difficulty Easy the first time (+2 levels if no harm is intended), +3 per additional use; roll control. Failure: lose 1D Character Points or the dark side takes 1D from an attribute or Force skill; 0D means death.

dark_side.fallen: Normally a character with more than six Dark Side Points becomes a gamemaster character. Optional rules to keep playing: no Character Points for adventuring (one per Dark Side Point instead); Force Points only regained when spent on evil at a dramatically appropriate moment, otherwise lost; the gamemaster secretly rolls 2D against the number of evil acts in the adventure to decide if a Dark Side Point is gained.

returning_to_the_light.requirement: Spend a Force Point selflessly at a dramatically appropriate moment (often a heroic sacrifice); the gamemaster decides.
returning_to_the_light.cost: Lose all Force Points and Character Points; Dark Side Points drop to five; the character should atone.

atonement.ways: Chosen according to belief (Jedi fast, reflect, meditate). Actively prevent evil, preferably non-violently: preserve life, preserve the right to knowledge and enlightenment, preserve peace and harmony, defend the defenseless.
atonement.note: Atonement starts over if a Dark Side Point is received during it.

optional_rules.dramatic_force_use: Use a power you do not know for 10 Character Points and one Force Point, after having witnessed it, in a dramatic situation. Points are lost even on failure; using it selfishly gives two Dark Side Points. (p.175)
optional_rules.learning_difficulty_instead_of_required_: Roll willpower against a learning difficulty: 5 for powers without prerequisites, +5 per prerequisite power. Failure: wait at least a month (or never, at the gamemaster's discretion) and the Character Points are lost. Example: absorb/dissipate energy 5; combat sense (two prerequisites) 15. (p.175)
optional_rules.slow_progression_into_darkness: Each Dark Side Point adds a negative personality trait (chosen or rolled on 4D from a list of 21 traits such as Arrogant, Deceitful, Hateful, Paranoia, Power-hungry). (p.178)

force_traditions.tyia_example: A Tyia student learning control at 1D automatically learns hibernation trance and emptiness (Easy for Tyia) plus three more control powers; all alter powers are one difficulty level higher; all powers take at least one minute. Other traditions (Witches of Dathomir, Ossus) must be defined by the gamemaster. (p.174)

character_movement.move_score: Meters per round while walking (most humans 10). Moving is an action; once per round. Running/walking rolls running or Dexterity; swimming uses swimming or Strength; climbing uses climbing/jumping or Strength. Unusual movement (swimming, climbing) is normally one-third of Move.
character_movement.roll: Roll >= the terrain difficulty number to move without problem; lower is a movement failure.

speeds.easy_terrain: free action in Very Easy, Easy and Moderate terrain: no roll, no multiple-action penalty
speeds.hard_terrain: in Difficult, Very Difficult and Heroic terrain roll running with the difficulty reduced one level

speeds.easy_terrain: an action; automatic in Very Easy, Easy and Moderate terrain
speeds.hard_terrain: roll running for Difficult, Very Difficult and Heroic terrain

speeds.easy_terrain: roll running in Very Easy, Easy and Moderate terrain
speeds.hard_terrain: Difficult becomes Very Difficult, Very Difficult becomes Heroic, Heroic becomes Heroic +10

speeds.restriction: May do nothing else that round, including dodge or parry.
speeds.easy_terrain: difficulty +1 level in Very Easy, Easy and Moderate terrain
speeds.hard_terrain: difficulty +2 levels in Difficult, Very Difficult and Heroic terrain

character_movement.partial_moves: After choosing a speed, move anywhere between half and the full distance of that speed (all-out with Move 10: 20 to 40 m).
character_movement.acceleration: Characters may change speed up to two levels per round (cautious -> high is allowed, cautious -> all-out is not; all-out cannot drop to cautious or stop in one round).

encumbrance.rule: A character can carry one medium-sized object per pip of Strength (1D = 3 pips; Strength 3D+2 = 11 objects). Carrying too much applies the long-distance movement and stamina rules.
encumbrance.medium_items: Fatigues, boots, partial armor, helmet, a main weapon, three grenades, three days' rations, about half a dozen small objects (power tools, power packs, a secondary weapon), backpack, comm gear, scanner, explosives, portable computer, and similar.

long_distance.all_out: Stamina roll every minute (first Very Easy, +1 level each roll). Failure: rest twice as long as moved all-out.
long_distance.high_speed: Stamina roll every 10 minutes (first Very Easy, +1 level each roll). Failure: rest twice as long as moved at high speed.
long_distance.marching: Cruising march: Very Easy stamina check every 3 hours (+1 level each), assuming 5-15 minute breaks; marching continuously: every 2 hours. One hour of sleep per stamina check made restores vigor. Terrain may modify the difficulty.
long_distance.terrain_checks: Movement checks for terrain every 3 hours (2 on a forced march); some terrain forces cautious movement.

terrain_difficulty_characters.examples: Flat, clear, even ground; clear walkways. Swimming: calm water.
Flat but naturally uneven ground (fields, yards) with a few small obstacles. Swimming: minor obstacles or moderate currents.
Rough ground or many obstacles (large holes, rocks, thickets). Swimming: many obstacles or a very confined area.
Densely packed area (panicked crowd, thick forest); very rough ground, darkened tunnels, falling boulders. Swimming in a very rough storm or among predators.
Very dangerous terrain: minefield, crawl-way with whirling fans, a starship breaking apart. Swimming in a dangerous storm with large waves.
Virtually impassable: avalanche, corridor of falling debris and exploding consoles, swimming in a tidal wave or hurricane.

maneuver_modifiers.rule: The terrain number covers straight-line movement and simple turns. Harder maneuvers (tight beams, grabbing something mid-run) add modifiers. Crossing into other skills (jump a ditch, climb a wall) needs a separate climbing/jumping roll after the movement roll.

levels.meaning: takes a little effort and coordination
a lot of concentration; very difficult while moving quickly
very, very difficult while moving quickly

rows.effect: -1D to all actions for the rest of the round (plus multiple-action penalties).
Moves only half the Move; -3D to all actions for the rest of the round and -1D next round.
Falls halfway through the Move, ends kneeling; no actions for the rest of the round; -2D to all actions next round.
Falls a quarter of the way through the Move; no actions for the rest of the round and next round; collision damage reduced by 3D (so 1D if all-out, otherwise none).
Falls at a bad angle; collision damage +2D.

movement_failures_characters.damage_resolution: Roll against the character's Strength as in the damage rules (see damage-healing.json).

starship_categories.summary: Large combat vessels, typically over 100 m, large crews, shields and many weapon emplacements.
Small combat craft with a crew of one or two, almost no cargo, powerful weapons and fast sublight speed.
Any starship not built for combat: scouts, freighters, shuttles, yachts, liners; many are refitted with weapons and shields.

space-travel.skill_attribute_note: The text (p.120) says each piloting skill can fall back on the Technical attribute; the skills chapter lists these skills under Mechanical (see errata).
sublight_benchmarks: 5 minutes: orbit to a safe hyperspace jump point.
30 minutes: planet to one of its moons.
2 to 6 hours: planet to the nearest planet in the system.
10 to 48 hours: star to the outer limits of a system (about 15 hours for a representative system).
A micro jump between planets takes about an hour and needs very precise coordinates.

hyperdrive.multiplier: Class rating; lower is faster. Trip time = route duration (for a x1 drive) x ship's multiplier. Class 0.5 halves it, class 2 doubles it. Most civilian ships x2 or worse, many military ships and starfighters x1, Millennium Falcon x0.5.
hyperdrive.backup: Many ships carry a slow backup drive (x10, x15 or more) to limp to a spaceport.
hyperdrive.example: Tatooine to Bespin 16 hours: x2 drive 32 hours; x1 16 hours; x0.5 8 hours.
hyperdrive.hazards: Contact with an object's hyperspace shadow destroys a ship; mass shadow sensors shut the drive down but are not fully reliable. Changing course in hyperspace is nearly suicidal.

steps: Make the calculations for the jump.
astrogation.base_difficulty: Most trips Moderate; easy trips can be Easy (Coruscant to Chandrila); perilous routes much higher (the Kessel Run needs at least five Very Difficult rolls).
astrogation.verified_against: PDF page 125 (the text export misaligns this table)

modifiers.situation: No nav computer or astromech droid
Each extra hour taken on the journey
Each hour saved on the journey

results.result: The jump goes without a hitch.
The ship cannot enter hyperspace; a new roll is needed.

calculation_time.time: 1 round; difficulty doubled; roll each round until success or a mishap

calculation_time.case: Never jumped to that system before

calculation_time.time: 1 day to fix position and compute coordinates

sample_durations.time: a few hours to a few days (1D)
add 1D of the base time unit

hyperdrive_start_up_optional.rule: Base time x the ship's hyperdrive multiplier; included in plotting time if the calculation is made in space.

astrogation.stopping_jumps: Lightly damaged ship +5, heavily damaged +10, each controls ionized result from an ion cannon +5, a tractor beam adds its damage roll (with scale adjustment) to the difficulty; hasty jumps double the difficulty. All are cumulative.

rows.name: Hyperdrive cut-out and damaged
rows.effect: Avoids a collision but damages the engines; a Moderate repair roll (capital ship repair, space transports repair or starfighter repair) fixes the main drive, otherwise use the backup drive.

rows.name: Radiation fluctuations
rows.effect: Journey time changes by +1D or -1D hours per point missed (miss by 3: up to 3D hours).

rows.name: Hyperdrive cut-out
rows.effect: A mass shadow throws the ship into realspace; calculate a new route from there.

rows.name: Off course
rows.effect: Emerges in the wrong system; plot a new trip.

rows.name: Mynocks
rows.effect: Mynocks on the power cables; journey +1D days.

rows.name: Close call
rows.effect: Another system (sublight drives, nav computer, escape pods, weapons) is damaged; the journey completes but repairs are needed on arrival.

rows.name: Collision, heavy damage
rows.effect: The ship drops to realspace heavily damaged with a ruptured hull and must be abandoned. Characters in the ruptured area need a Moderate survival total to reach survival suits in one round; otherwise a stamina check each round (Easy, Moderate, Difficult, Very Difficult, Heroic, Heroic +10...) to avoid passing out.

sensors.difficulty: Based on range to the target, modified by anything that affects readings (a ship in open space is easy; one hiding in an asteroid belt is hard). Details in the skills chapter.

modes.description: Only receives information about the ship's immediate vicinity.
Pulses in all directions; longer range and higher dice than passive.
One fire arc only (front, left, right or back); greater range and dice than scan, no information on the other arcs.
A small area; the number is the radius in space units; maximum is the search range; no information elsewhere.

sensors.listing_format: Range in space units / dice added to the sensors skill, e.g. Passive 15/0D, Scan 25/1D, Search 40/2D, Focus 1/3D.
countermeasures: Hide behind a planet or other large body (sensors are line of sight).
Run silent: power down engines, weapons and shields; usually no more than five minutes before life support must be cut.
Jam: flood an area with static (reveals that someone is jamming).
Sensor decoys, sensor masks (add dice to the difficulty to detect), false transponder codes.

space-travel.communications: Only work in realspace. HoloNet transceivers (rare, military), hypertransceivers (military and large private ships), subspace transceivers (most ships; an X-wing's reaches 25 light years, up to 100+ with power; also for distress signals), comms (speed-of-light ship-to-ship and ship-to-planet), intercomms. Finding a signal without its frequency is very hard.

operating_license.requires: background check on the owner, brief inspection, transponder code verification

captains_accredited_license.requires: oral, written and flight tests, documented time in space, background check (BoSS often waives flight time and most testing for the expediter fee)

arms_load_out_permit.note: One permit per weapon or boosted shield system; upgraded weapons need new permits; ships without one can be impounded.

starport_costs.docking_fee_per_day: most standard class or larger: 50 credits per standard day; a busy Imperial/Republic class port up to 150
starport_costs.standard_restock_and_maintenance: Automatic at standard class or better within about a day of landing, with fees charged unless declined.
starport_costs.restocking_fee: base fee x total crew and passenger capacity x days of consumables renewed; base fee about 10 credits on busy routes, up to 35 at isolated ports
starport_costs.maintenance_overhaul: After every 20 hyperspace jumps; about 1,000 credits on average, up to 5,000 for heavily modified or heavily used ships. Skipping it is up to the gamemaster (a complication on the Wild Die might cause a misjump or hyperdrive blow-out).
starport_costs.traffic_fines: Deviating from an assigned approach course: 50 to 200 credits.

speed-conversion.description: All-out speed in km/h for a Move score (characters or vehicles). High speed (a character's running) is half the all-out km/h; cruising (walking) is one quarter; cautious (slow walk) is one eighth.
speed-conversion.formula: all-out km/h = Move x 2.88 (table values are rounded)
speed-conversion.validated: All 43 rows checked against Move x 2.88 (within 5% or 10 km/h) and for monotonic order.
speed-conversion.example: Move 350 -> all-out 1,000 km/h; high 500; cruising 250; cautious 125.

movement.space_score: Moves in Space units per round at cruising speed. Slow ships 2-3, average freighters 5-6, fastest starfighters 11-12. Moving is an action; once per round.
movement.roll: Pilot rolls the ship's piloting skill (capital ship piloting, space transports or starfighter piloting) plus the ship's maneuverability code; >= difficulty or movement failure.

speeds.note: Round up. Free action in Very Easy/Easy/Moderate space (no roll); in harder space roll with the difficulty one level lower.
An action; automatic in Very Easy/Easy/Moderate space; roll for Difficult or worse.
Roll in all space; Difficult becomes Very Difficult, Very Difficult becomes Heroic, Heroic becomes Heroic +10.
No other action (no starship dodges, no weapons; shields at the gamemaster's discretion). Difficulty +1 level in easy space, +2 levels in hard space.

movement.acceleration: One level per round (high speed can go to cruising or all-out, not to cautious or a stop).
movement.partial_moves: Anywhere from half to the full distance of the chosen speed.
movement.long_distance: All-out: hull code roll every 10 minutes (first Very Easy, +1 level each). High speed: every hour. Fail by 1-10: strain, rest twice as long; fail by 11+: mechanical failure (Moderate repair roll, at least an hour).

terrain_difficulty.examples: Clear space with no navigational hazards.
Near other ships (orbiting a station); minor obstacles such as a small dispersed asteroid belt.
Crowded space (busy spacedock staging area); moderate debris; the Death Star's artificial canyon.
Starfighter combat with many ships close by; areas clogged with debris or asteroids.
Space densely packed with ships or debris.
Almost impossible: inside the Death Star to the reactor core; Hoth's asteroid field.

maneuver_modifiers.meaning: very difficult, needs a very talented or lucky pilot

movement_failures.effect: Pilot -1D to all actions for the rest of the round.
Half the Space move; pilot -3D this round and -1D next.
A quarter of the Space move, then out of control: no control this round and next.
If anything to hit: collision damage -3D; otherwise spins out of control (no control this round and next).
Normal collision damage if anything to hit; otherwise spins out of control.
Collision damage +4D if anything to hit; otherwise spins out of control.

movement.collision_notes: Roll collision damage against the hull code roll; account for scale; reduce by -1D, -2D or more if the ship hits something very light.

combat.attack: Difficulty by the weapon's range in Space units; roll starship gunnery (starfighter-scale weapons) or capital ship gunnery (capital-scale weapons) plus the weapon's fire control; >= difficulty hits; roll damage. All starships provide full cover.
combat.reaction: Starship dodge: piloting skill + maneuverability becomes the new difficulty. Full reaction (only action of the round): the roll is added to every attack's difficulty.
combat.weapons_rules: Starship weapons use the fire control, ammo, fire rate, blast radius and scale rules of the Combat chapter, and ranges, crew and fire arcs of the Movement chapter. 'Range' is in Space units; 'Atmosphere Range' applies in an atmosphere or when firing into one from orbit.
combat.fire_linked: Statistics are for fire-linked groups (X-wing: four laser cannons, 6D together). Fired separately, apply the combined-action bonus in reverse: four cannons subtract -1D+2, so each does 4D+1.

weapon_types.laser_cannons_and_turbolasers: Laser cannons are standard on starfighter-scale ships; turbolasers are capital-scale.
weapon_types.ion_cannons: Interfere with electrical and computer systems, cause no physical damage, and ignore shields (only the hull code resists).

missiles_bombs_torpedoes.rule: Difficulty rises with the target's speed.

tractor_beams.rule: Hit with a normal attack. Roll the beam's damage against the target's hull code. A captured ship that does not resist is reeled in 5 Space units per round. If it resists: hull code higher breaks free; beam equal or higher reels it in and may damage the drives.

shields.types: Particle shields deflect physical objects (asteroids, missiles, torpedoes); they are lowered to launch fighters or fire missiles/torpedoes, which gives -2D hull code. Losing the main generator loses particle shields. Energy/ray shields also exist.
shields.use: Shields are a reaction skill (starship shields; capital ship shields). Split the ship's shield dice among the four fire arcs (front, back, left, right). Hits from a covered arc add those shield dice to the hull code to resist damage.
shields.example: Hull 4D, shields 2D all on the back arc: attacks from the back resist with 6D. Split 1D front and 1D back (Moderate): 5D against either, 4D against the sides.
shields.capital_ship_option: When shield dice are lost, roll 1D per die lost to set the difficulty of shunting the overload (capital ship shields). Success: only controls ionized. Failure: roll the lost dice against hull dice as damage. A Wild Die complication or a 'shields lost' result makes the shield module explode.

called_shots_on_ships.rule: A weapon cannot target a location on a ship of a lower scale than itself (a capital weapon can hit a capital ship's engines but not a starfighter's).

difficulty_modifiers.location: Primary section (conning tower, engines, landing bay, main body)
Subsection (gun battery, one engine, shield generators, command section)
Specific location (a gun, the bridge, a thruster, an exhaust port)

power_control_optional.capacity: A ship has power for all systems and can channel up to +2D extra to any system from other systems. Raw power does not help computers (nav, targeting) but can boost comms range or active sensor scans. All-out ships cannot fire or maneuver and may not use shields.

base_difficulty.condition: Simple rerouting (one system to one recipient)

starship_damage.resolution: Roll damage (attack or collision) against the hull code roll. Lower: no damage. Equal or higher: use the chart.
starship_damage.shields_blown: -1D from shields until repaired; with none left, controls ionized.
starship_damage.controls_ionized: -1D from maneuverability, shields, weapon fire control and damage for the rest of this round and the next. As many ionized results as maneuverability dice freeze the controls for two rounds (same speed and direction, no turning, weapons, shields or other actions); piloting rolls must still be made or the ship crashes (or spins if nothing to hit).

results.effect: -1D maneuverability (if already 0D: -1 Move).
One weapon emplacement (random) destroyed; gunners take damage.
One weapon emplacement (random) inoperative: lightly damaged.
Hyperdrive damaged: double astrogation calculation times; a one-round jump adds +10 to the difficulty. Fix: one hour and a Moderate repair roll (capital ship, space transports or starfighter repair).
-1D shields (if none: controls ionized).
-1 Move.

heavily_damaged.note: Lightly or heavily damaged again becomes severely damaged.

results.effect: -2D maneuverability (if already 0D: -2 Move).
Weapons system in one fire arc (random) inoperative: all weapons of that type in that arc.
Weapons system destroyed: all weapons of one type in the same arc; gunners take damage.
Hyperdrive damaged: +10 to all astrogation difficulties until fixed (Moderate repair, one hour).
-2D shields (if none: 2 controls ionized).
-2 Move.

severely_damaged.note: Lightly, heavily or severely damaged again is destroyed.

results.effect: Dead in space: all drives and maneuvering systems destroyed.
Overloaded generator: explodes in 1D rounds unless shut down.
Hyperdrives (main and backup) disabled until fixed (Moderate repair, one hour).
All weapons lose power; roll 1D: 1-4 severely damaged but repairable, 5-6 all weapons destroyed.
Structural damage: the ship disintegrates; the crew has 1D rounds to evacuate.
Destroyed: disintegrates or explodes.

starship_damage.destroyed: Instantly destroyed; everyone aboard is killed.

lost_moves.effect: No all-out; limited to high speed.
Sublight drives disabled; dead in space.

vehicle_movement.rule: A vehicle has a Move (meters per round at cruising speed) and moves once per round (an action). Pilot rolls the vehicle's operation skill (repulsorlift operation for most speeders; walker operation, ground vehicle operation, hover vehicle operation, swoop operation otherwise) plus the vehicle's maneuverability code, or Mechanical if unskilled. Roll >= terrain difficulty or suffer a movement failure.

speeds.note: Free action in Very Easy/Easy/Moderate terrain (no roll). In harder terrain roll with the difficulty reduced one level.
An action; automatic in Very Easy/Easy/Moderate terrain; roll for Difficult, Very Difficult, Heroic.
Roll in all terrain; Difficult becomes Very Difficult, Very Difficult becomes Heroic, Heroic becomes Heroic +10.
Pilot may do nothing else (no vehicle dodges, no weapons). Difficulty +1 level in easy terrain, +2 levels in hard terrain.

vehicle_movement.acceleration: Vehicles change speed one level per round (unlike characters, who change two).
vehicle_movement.partial_moves: Anywhere from half to the full distance of the chosen speed.

long_distance.all_out: Body strength roll every 10 minutes (first Very Easy, +1 level each). Fail by 1-10: strain, must rest twice as long as it moved all-out. Fail by 11+: mechanical failure needing a Moderate repair roll and at least an hour.
long_distance.high_speed: Body strength roll every hour (first Very Easy, +1 level each).

terrain_difficulty_vehicles.examples: Flat artificial surfaces such as roads; light traffic; repulsorlift flight over any flat, stable surface.
Smooth surfaces with minor obstacles; moderate traffic; repulsorlift over uneven terrain or in moderate traffic.
Heavy traffic at high speed; rough terrain or an intense storm; repulsorlift over very uneven terrain or in severely limited visibility.
Very rough terrain (mountainside, crater field, meteor storm); chase in heavy traffic; flight through thick forests or Beggar's Canyon.
Driving through a city during an earthquake or fierce battle; flight in similar circumstances.
Verging on impossible: thick swamps with vines at every turn; racing through an immense drilling machine.

levels.meaning: very difficult, needs a very talented or lucky pilot

examples.effect: Slams brakes, spins and slides: moves half its Move and ends facing the opposite direction.
Climb or dive at 45 degrees or more.
A turn over 45 degrees while keeping high speed.
Jumping off a bridge, cliff or ramp; depends on distance and landing.
At cruising speed or less, turn up to 360 degrees without changing inertia.

rows.effect: Pilot -1D to all actions for the rest of the round.
Vehicle makes half its Move; pilot -3D to all actions this round and -1D next round.
Completes a quarter of its Move, then spins out of control: no movement for the rest of the round and the next round; may move again in two rounds if not damaged by a collision.
Glances off an obstacle; collision damage -3D. If there is nothing to hit, spins out and cannot move this round and next.
Normal collision damage. With nothing to hit, may spin, tumble or flip (gamemaster).
Collision damage +4D. With nothing to hit, flips or suffers another serious collision.

notes: Roll collision damage against the vehicle's body strength roll (use damage caps when scales differ).
Soft obstacles (wooden fence, thick bushes) may reduce damage by -1D, -2D or more; a hardened wall gives full damage.
Example from the book: high speed (6D) + major collision (+4D) + head-on (+3D) = 13D.

vehicle_combat.attack: Difficulty by range; roll vehicle blasters (or Dexterity) plus fire control; >= difficulty hits; roll damage.
vehicle_combat.reaction: Vehicle dodge: pilot's operation skill + the vehicle's maneuverability code becomes the new difficulty. Full reaction (only action that round, not even moving): the roll is added to the difficulty of every attack against the vehicle.
vehicle_combat.modifiers: All Combat chapter modifiers apply; also scale and cover (None, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, Full).
vehicle_combat.weapon_ranges: If a weapon lists four ranges, the first is point-blank (Very Easy); anything closer is below point-blank and Very Difficult. Example blaster cannon 10-50/100/200/500.
vehicle_combat.crew: Crew N = number of gunners needed; only one rolls the attack skill. No crew listing: the pilot can fire it.
vehicle_combat.fire_arcs: Front, back, left, right, turret (turret = any direction).

ramming.rule: Pass very close to the target during the move. +10 to the movement difficulty and a separate action (extra -1D to the pilot).
outcomes: Roll higher than the +10 difficulty: ram hits.
Roll lower than the original movement difficulty: movement failure.
Roll between the original difficulty and the +10 difficulty: move succeeds but the ram misses.
ramming.damage: Attacker takes sideswipe damage (-3D); the victim takes T-bone damage (normal). The target may make a vehicle dodge.

complex_maneuvers.name: Attack Pattern Delta
complex_maneuvers.summary: Speeders approach a walker single file head-on, strafe, then veer off in different directions.
complex_maneuvers.game_notes: Each pilot makes an extra Easy repulsorlift operation roll to form up. Each following speeder gets +1D when attackers straight ahead shoot at it; the lead speeder gets no bonus.

complex_maneuvers.name: Bantha Decoy
complex_maneuvers.summary: Lead speeder attacks and banks away so the walker turns its guns, exposing its head and neck to a trailing speeder.
complex_maneuvers.game_notes: If the lead speeder hits, the walker's commander makes a free opposed tactics or Perception roll against the lead pilot. If the commander loses, the trailing speeder gets +1D+2 to hit and the walker's gunners get +5 difficulty against the trailing speeder.

vehicle_damage.resolution: Roll the damage (weapon or collision) against the vehicle's body strength roll. Lower: no damage. Equal or higher: use the chart.
vehicle_damage.shields_blown: -1D from the shields total until repaired; with no shield dice left (or none), treat as controls ionized.
vehicle_damage.controls_ionized: -1D from maneuverability, fire control, weapon damage and shield dice for the rest of this round and the next (body strength unaffected). If the number of controls ionized results equals the vehicle's maneuverability dice, controls freeze for two rounds: same speed and direction, no turning, weapons, shields or other actions; the pilot must keep rolling operation (a difficulty is set) or the vehicle crashes.

results.effect: -1D maneuverability (if already 0D: -1 Move).
One weapon (random) destroyed; gunners take damage.
-1 Move.
-2D maneuverability until repaired (if already 0D: -2 Move).
-2 Move.

heavily_damaged.note: A heavily damaged vehicle that is lightly or heavily damaged again becomes severely damaged.

results.effect: Destroyed powerplant: ground vehicle at high/all-out speed crashes; at cruising/cautious it rolls to a stop; flying vehicles plummet and the pilot needs an operation roll (minimum Moderate) to land.
Overloaded generator: explodes in 1D rounds; minimum Moderate to crash-land or stop safely.
All weapons shut down.
Structural damage: 1D rounds to eject or crash-land (minimum Moderate).
Destroyed or crashes from complete loss of control.

severely_damaged.note: A severely damaged vehicle damaged again is destroyed.

vehicle_damage.destroyed: Immediately destroyed; all passengers take damage.

lost_moves.effect: Cannot move all-out; limited to high speed.

passenger_damage.rule: Gamemaster judges whether passengers are hurt; damage is character-scale.

vehicle_damage.falling: Damage matches the scale of the faller; same table as character falling (see damage-healing.json). Increase a couple of levels on high gravity worlds, decrease on low gravity worlds.

sections.title: Characters (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are the book's printed pages.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Start from a **template** (Chapter 23: smuggler, Rebel pilot, merc, Wookiee...) or build a new one. Copy the template's die codes, Move and equipment, name the character, and finish four steps. The gamemaster approves any change. (p.18-19)

sections.title: Finishing a template
sections.text:
Give the character a name, height, weight, sex, age and look. Every character starts with **5 Character Points**. (p.21) Then:
1. **Pick skills** 2. **Decide Force sensitivity** 3. **Spend credits** 4. **Pick Force powers**. (p.21)

sections.title: 1. Pick skills
sections.text:
- Beginning characters have **7D** to place in skills: add **1D or 2D** to any skill shown on the template. Unimproved skills use the attribute's die code. (p.21)
- Other skills may be added with the gamemaster's permission. **Force skills** (control, sense, alter) can be improved only if the template already lists them. (p.21)
- Worked example in the book: Dexterity 4D, +1D blaster = 5D; +2D dodge = 6D; Mechanical 2D+2, +2D space transports = 4D+2; Perception 3D, +1D search = 4D. (p.21)

**Specializations** (p.21): spend **1D** of beginning skill dice to get **three** specializations, each +1D over the base skill (or over the attribute if the skill is unimproved). A specialization is rolled only for its specific item or knowledge. Example: blaster 5D, blaster: blaster pistol 6D; alien species: Wookiees at 3D+2 (Knowledge 2D+2 + 1D).

**Advanced skills** (marked `(A)`; p.22): cannot be attempted without the skill. If the character meets the prerequisite skills, beginning dice may go into them; an advanced skill **starts at 1D**, not at the attribute. When a prerequisite skill is rolled, add the advanced skill's dice. Example: (A) medicine needs first aid 5D; first aid 5D + (A) medicine 1D rolls 6D on first aid, but only 1D on surgery. Cross off unused advanced skills.

sections.title: 2. Force sensitivity
sections.text: Yes = starts with **2 Force Points**; No = **1**. Force-sensitive characters must behave morally and honorably or the dark side dominates them. (p.22) Becoming Force-sensitive later: 20 Character Points (see Advancement).

sections.title: 3. Spend credits
sections.text: Templates with starting credits buy gear from the Equipment chapter; the gamemaster may attach strings (for example a debt on a ship). (p.22)

sections.title: 4. Force powers
sections.text: A Force-sensitive character who starts with any Force skill knows at least one power; choose with the gamemaster in the Force chapter. (p.22)

sections.title: Creating a new template
sections.text:
(p.23-25) Data: `tables/character-creation-advancement.json` (`creation.new_template`).
1. Choose a **type** (short title, include species if alien) and write background and personality.
2. Choose a **species** (Aliens chapter, or droid via the Droids chapter).
3. **Attribute dice** = the species' Attribute Dice **+ 6D** (humans 12D + 6D = 18D).
4. Split them among the six attributes within each species' **minimum/maximum** die codes (humans 2D/4D). A die can be divided into three pips; +3 becomes the next full die. (p.23)
5. Write down **special abilities** that matter in play; creation-only abilities (skill bonuses and limits) only matter now. (p.23-24)
6. **Move**: species list "start/maximum" (humans 10/12); the character starts at the first. (p.24)
7. **Force-sensitive?** yes/no/leave blank. Optional Force skills cost **1D of attribute dice per 1D** and need gamemaster permission; attributes cannot go below the species minimum. (p.24)
8. Optional starting **Dark Side Points** (agree with the gamemaster). (p.24)
9. **List skills** under each attribute (only the ones to pick now; 7D total starting skill dice). (p.24)
10. **Starting credits** (optional, 2D roll): Poor 2D x 100, Average 2D x 250, Wealthy 2D x 400. (p.24)
11. **Starting equipment**: reasonable list; the gamemaster has the final say and may add disadvantages such as debts. (p.24-25)
12. Show the template to the gamemaster for approval, then do "Finishing a template". (p.25)

Changing a template's species: re-check attribute dice, limits, special abilities and Move against the new species. (p.23)

sections.title: Character advancement
sections.text:
Character Points are awarded after each adventure and spent between adventures. (p.25) Data: `tables/character-creation-advancement.json` (`advancement`).

| Improve | Cost | Limit and notes |
|---|---|---|
| Skill, +1 pip | number before the "D" (3D+2 -> 4D costs 3) | one pip per skill between adventures |
| Specialization, +1 pip | half the number before the "D", rounded up | separate from the base skill (neither raises the other) |
| Advanced skill, +1 pip | 2 x number before the "D" | train always |
| New skill/specialization | enough to reach +1 pip above the attribute (attribute 3D -> 3 points) | training unless the attribute was used for it last adventure |
| Learn advanced skill | usually 2 points for 1D, prerequisites required | training weeks apply |
| Attribute, +1 pip | 10 x number before the "D" | all skills under it (not advanced) also +1 pip; ceiling check below |
| Move, +1 meter | current Move | up to the species maximum |
| Become Force-sensitive | 20 | no training; +1 Force Point; permanent |

**Attribute ceiling check** (p.27): after training, the player rolls the new attribute code; the gamemaster rolls the species' maximum for it. Player roll **<=** gamemaster roll: it increases. Higher: it does not, and half the Character Points are returned. (Example: human Dex 4D -> 4D+1 for 40 points; player 17 vs gamemaster 4D roll 15: fails, 20 points returned.)

**Training time** (p.26):
- Skill or specialization **used in the last adventure**: no training time.
- Otherwise: **1 day per Character Point with a teacher, 2 days without**. Each extra Character Point cuts one day (minimum 1 day). The skill improves only when training finishes; one skill at a time, and not while off adventuring.
- Advanced skill: **1 week per point with a teacher, 2 weeks without**; 1 Character Point per day cut; minimum 1 week.
- Attribute and Move: **1 week per point with a teacher, 2 without**; one extra Character Point per day cut; minimum 1 week.
- **Teacher**: skill (or the exact specialization) at least equal to the value the student will reach. The gamemaster need not provide teachers; rare skills and advanced skills may cost service, favors or payment. (p.26)
- The gamemaster may allow learning during a real lull in an adventure. (p.25)

Special abilities may be improvable under conditions stated in their own description. (p.28)

sections.title: Optional rules (only if the gamemaster allows)
Advantages and disadvantages (p.28-30)
sections.text: Add the modifiers of the chosen entries: a positive total **adds** starting skill dice; a negative total **removes** them. Disadvantages give dice (+), advantages cost dice (-). Example: Debt +2D, Quick Draw -2D, Released Convict +1D = +1D. Full list with effects: `tables/advantages-disadvantages.json` (36 entries).

sections.title: Contacts (p.30-31)
sections.text: Optional: up to three starting contacts (**one friend, two acquaintances**). Friends risk much for you; acquaintances give occasional favors when the risk is low. Types: family, conditional, professional, influential. Contacts should be limited in what they can do and must pass the gamemaster's scrutiny.

sections.title: Enemies and rivals (p.31)
sections.text: Built the same way as contacts. Enemies actively oppose you; rivals compete for the same resource and may become allies.

sections.title: Detailing a character (roleplaying aids)
sections.text: The book (p.19-20) suggests defining: physical description, background (known to you and the gamemaster only), personality (good and bad points), objectives (immediate, short or long-term) and connections with other characters (friends, relatives, employees, joint ship ownership, travelling companions, mentors, rivals, same homeworld, classmates, reputation, love; love only if players choose it).

sections.title: Combat and injuries (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. Combat uses 5-second rounds (`core-mechanics.md#scenes-rounds`).

sections.title: An attack in four steps
sections.text:
1. Determine the difficulty number (by range or the melee weapon's difficulty, plus modifiers).
2. The attacker rolls the attack skill (or its attribute if the skill is unimproved).
3. Roll **>=** difficulty: the attack hits (the book says "higher" once on p.89 but "equal to or greater" everywhere else, see E-023).
4. Roll damage; the target rolls Strength (plus armor) to resist. (p.89)

sections.title: Ranged attacks
sections.text:
Skill by weapon: blaster, bowcaster, firearms (slugthrowers), grenade (grenades, thermal detonators), thrown weapons, missile weapons (launchers), vehicle blasters, blaster artillery. Check the weapon's description for its skill and specialization. (p.89)
- Weapon stats: damage code and three ranges in metres, e.g. blaster pistol `4D, 3-10/30/120`. Closer than the first number is point-blank. (p.89)
- Difficulty by range: **point-blank Very Easy, short Easy, medium Moderate, long Difficult**; beyond long range the weapon cannot hit. Then the gamemaster picks the exact number. (p.89)
- Quick range estimates and the other modifiers: `tables/combat-modifiers.json`.

sections.title: Melee and brawling
sections.text: Melee combat and lightsaber use their skills (or Dexterity). Each melee weapon has its own difficulty. Brawling (bare hands, claws) is Very Easy and rolls Strength if unimproved. (p.90)

sections.title: Reactions
sections.text:
(p.90-91; also `core-mechanics.md#reactions` and `skills.md#dex-groups`)
- **Dodge**: any ranged attack (Dexterity if unskilled).
- **Melee parry**: you hold a melee weapon and are attacked by melee or brawling. **+5** to the parry if the attacker is unarmed with no sharp natural weapons.
- **Brawling parry**: you are unarmed. If the attacker uses a weapon or sharp natural tools, the attacker gets **+10** to hit.
- **Lightsaber**: parry melee, brawling or lightsaber attacks while wielding one.
- **Vehicle dodge / starship dodge**: roll the vehicle's operation or the starship's piloting skill (Mechanical if unskilled).
- A reaction roll becomes the attacker's **new difficulty** for all attacks of that type for the rest of the round, even if lower than the original (a poor reaction can make you easier to hit). Apply multiple-action penalties. Example: dodge 27 means every ranged attacker needs 27; a brawling attack stays at its own difficulty. (p.90-91)
- **Full reaction**: dodge, parry, lightsaber, vehicle or starship dodge as your **only action all round**; the roll is **added** to the difficulty of **every** attack against you that round (example: dodge 27 on difficulties 13 and 8 gives 40 and 35). You cannot parry a type of attack you did not react to. (p.91)

sections.title: Weapon handling
sections.text:
- **Draw / ready / reload**: one action each. Drawing and using in the same round costs the multiple-action penalty. (p.91-92, p.98)
- **Stun setting**: switching is an action (-1D to other actions). Most blasters have normal and stun. (p.92)
- **Fire control**: large weapons add their fire control dice to the attack roll (4D Dexterity + 2D = 6D). (p.92)
- **Ammo**: when shots equal the ammo rating, reload (one action unless stated). **Fire rate**: no rate = unlimited; whole number = maximum shots per round; fraction = fires only some rounds (1/2 = every other round). (p.92)
- **Blast radius**: everything inside takes damage; some weapons list damage by distance band (fragmentation grenade `5D/4D/3D/2D`, radius `0-2/4/6/10` m). (p.92)
- **Multiple weapons**: one-handed weapons can be used in both hands in the same round with the multiple-action penalty. (p.97)

sections.title: Grenades and thermal detonators
sections.text:
(p.92-93) Pick a target point; difficulty by range (+5 to +10 if the thrower cannot see the point). Hit: it lands on target. Miss: roll **1D for direction** (diagram on p.92) and distance **1D m** at point-blank/short, **2D** at medium, **3D** at long range.
- Contact grenades explode on impact; timed ones when the timer ends (under 5 seconds: at the end of the round of the throw).
- **Dodging a grenade** only means hitting the deck: the book's example has a throw of 17 and says the dodge needs **18 or higher** (higher than the throw), then no damage (see E-028).
- **Tossing one away**: roll grenade or Dexterity; it goes as far as the roll allows (the roll's range band) or at a chosen spot at normal difficulty.

sections.title: Cover and protection
sections.text: (p.93-94) Add cover modifiers to the difficulty to hit: smoke/light (+1D to +4D), partial cover **1/4 +1D, 1/2 +2D, 3/4 +4D**; full cover cannot be hit directly. If your roll beats the base difficulty but not base + cover, the shot hits the cover: roll damage against its **body strength**, find the damage state, and subtract dice from the damage that reaches the target (lightly damaged -4D, heavily -2D, severely -1D, destroyed full damage, not seriously damaged none). Tables: `combat-modifiers.json` (`cover`, `protection`).

sections.title: Armor
sections.text: Armor adds only to the **Strength roll to resist damage**, not to other Strength rolls. It can protect differently against physical and energy attacks and can penalize Dexterity and its skills (stormtrooper armor: +2D physical, +1D energy, -1D Dexterity). Armor is damaged when its wearer is: Wounded -1 pip, Incapacitated -1D, Mortally Wounded useless but repairable, Killed destroyed. (p.94)

sections.title: Damaged weapons and objects
sections.text: Hand weapons have body strength **2D**. Roll damage against it (damage-vs-body-strength table). Lightly damaged: -1D damage; heavily: -2D and +10 to all difficulties; severely: unusable but repairable; destroyed: not repairable. Works for other objects too. (p.95)

sections.title: Scale
sections.text: Character < speeder (2D) < walker (4D) < starfighter (6D) < capital (12D) < Death Star (24D). Use the difference ("adjusted modifier") only between different scales. **Lower attacks higher**: attacker adds it to the attack roll; target adds it to the roll to resist damage. **Higher attacks lower**: target adds it to its dodge; attacker adds it to damage. (p.95)

sections.title: Surprise
sections.text: Surprised characters cannot act, nor dodge or parry, against the attackers' first action. Ambushers roll sneak; targets roll search or Perception just before the ambush; equalling or beating **any** attacker's sneak means that attacker is spotted and no surprise. (p.96)

sections.title: Combat options
sections.text:
Data for all numeric modifiers: `tables/combat-modifiers.json`.
- **Acrobatic tricks**: do the trick and the attack the same turn; add half (rounded up) the difference between the trick's difficulty and the roll to the **damage** (not the attack roll); one trick affects one attack. (p.96)
- **Called shots** (small targets): +1D difficulty for a 10-50 cm target, +4D for 1-10 cm, +8D under 1 cm. Success: knock an item away, grab a limb, pin, or +1D damage. (p.96)
- **All attacks**: low gravity -1D, zero-G -2D, heavy gravity +3D difficulty; attacker blind +4D; target blind or attacked from behind -4D. (p.96)
- **Entangle**: on a hit, the target can only try to break free (an action): Strength or lifting >= the weapon's damage, or Dexterity or acrobatics >= its damage to slip free. (p.96)
- **Escape**: opposed Strength or lifting versus the holder; an action. (p.96)
- **Hit locations (optional)**: head +1D difficulty and +12 damage, heart +4D and +12, chest 0, arm +1D and -2, leg +1D and -1, hand +4D and -2; lasting penalties and a random-location table are in the data file. (p.96-97)
- **Knockout**: needs a called shot to the head with brawling or melee. Half damage; if at least two Wound levels remain after resistance, the target is unconscious for hours equal to the margin of the attack over the difficulty and takes half the Wound levels (round down). (p.97)
- **Prone / crouching**: crouched +1D difficulty (+2D if moving, and its Move or running roll is halved); prone -2D at point-blank/short, +2D at medium/long. (p.97)
- **Quick draw** (pistols, hold-outs, throwing knives; you do nothing else that round, not even dodge): split blaster dice into **speed draw** and **accuracy**. Highest speed-draw roll fires first and then rolls accuracy; the other may fire back only if not hurt. Several shots cost multiple-action penalties on both pools, and -1D per extra target. A stunned character loses -3D on later shots that round; a wounded or worse one cannot return fire. Against a dodger, a higher speed-draw roll means the dodge is ignored. (p.97-98)
- **Suppression fire** and **unwieldy weapons**: see the data file. (p.98)
- **Martial arts (optional)**: 20 techniques, one per full 1D of skill increase: `martial-arts.json`. (p.98-100)

sections.title: Damage and wounds
sections.text:
(p.100-101) Data: `tables/damage-healing.json`.
1. Attacker rolls damage; defender rolls Strength (+ armor). Damage higher than Strength: take the difference to the chart.
2. **Damage - Strength**: 1-3 Stunned, 4-8 Wounded, 9-12 Incapacitated, 13-15 Mortally Wounded, 16+ Killed.
3. **Stunned**: -1D for the rest of the round and the next; unconscious 2D minutes if stuns affecting you equal the number before the "D" in your Strength.
4. **Wounded**: prone, no actions this round, -1D until healed. **Wounded twice**: -2D. Wounded a third time: Incapacitated.
5. **Incapacitated**: prone, unconscious 10D minutes. **Mortally wounded**: unconscious; at the end of each round roll 2D, die if below the number of rounds you have been mortally wounded. **Killed**: dead.
6. Character Points or Force Points can raise the Strength roll to resist (up to 5 Character Points).
7. **Stun weapons**: anything worse than Stunned becomes unconscious for 2D minutes.

Optional damage rules (severe injuries, massive damage) and miscellaneous damage (falling, fire, electricity) are in the data file.

sections.title: Healing
sections.text:
(p.102-103) Data: `tables/damage-healing.json` (`healing`).
- **Natural**: rest 3 days (wounded or wounded twice), 2 weeks (incapacitated), 35 days (mortally wounded), then roll full Strength on the chart: it can heal, hold or worsen you. -1D if you work or adventure; +1D for doing nothing for twice the time.
- **Medpac**: first aid (or Technical) roll; Very Easy stunned/unconscious, Easy wounded/wounded twice, Moderate incapacitated, Difficult mortally wounded. Success heals one level. Missing by more than 10 locks out medpacs for 24 hours. Each extra use that day raises difficulty one level. Self-use costs an extra -1D.
- **Bacta tank**: needs (A) medicine (Very Easy); wounded 1D hours, incapacitated 4D hours, mortally wounded 1D days. Without (A) medicine a Heroic roll is needed and failure worsens the patient two levels.
- **Surgery**: (A) medicine with a kit and facility; Easy base; fully heals; failure worsens two levels.

sections.title: Core mechanics (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are the book's printed pages. English terms are the official ones.

sections.title: Die codes
sections.text:
- A die code `ND+P` means roll N six-sided dice, add them, then add P (the "pips"). `3D+1` = three dice + 1. (p.8-9)
- A skill starts at its attribute's code; trained skills add dice on top. (p.9)
- A bonus written as a die code (`+1D`) adds dice to the pool. A bonus written as a pip (`+2`) is added to the total. (p.73)

sections.title: Making a roll
sections.text:
- Roll skill dice (or the attribute if the skill is untrained) when an action is important and failure is possible. No roll for trivial actions. (p.73)
- Success: total **>=** difficulty number. (p.75)
- Opposed roll: both roll, higher wins; **a tie goes to the character who initiated the action**. (p.76)
- Modifiers are added to the character with the advantage for unusual situations, not for simple skill gaps. Guidelines: +1-5 slight, +6-10 good, +11-15 decisive, +16+ overpowering. (p.77) Data: `tables/difficulty-numbers.json`.

sections.title: Difficulty numbers
sections.text: Very Easy 1-5, Easy 6-10, Moderate 11-15, Difficult 16-20, Very Difficult 21-30, Heroic 31+ (Heroic +10 = 40-49, etc.). (p.75-76) The gamemaster chooses the exact number inside the level's range. Players need not be told the number. (p.77)

sections.title: The Wild Die
sections.text:
Applies to **every** die roll: skill, attribute, damage, initiative. (p.73)
1. On each roll, one die is designated the wild die (a different color; it is one of the dice, not extra).
2. Wild die shows 2-5: add normally.
3. Wild die shows 6: add it and roll it again; keep going while it shows 6.
4. Wild die shows 1 **on the first roll only**: tell the gamemaster, who picks one:
   - add the dice normally;
   - add normally to see whether the roll succeeded, but a *complication* occurs;
   - subtract the 1 **and** the highest other die.
5. When two kinds of dice are rolled at once (for example skill + starship maneuverability), only **one** die is the wild die. (p.73)

Complications are something related to the roll going wrong (even on a success); the gamemaster decides what. (p.73)

sections.title: Untrained use
sections.text: No dice in the skill: roll the governing attribute. Optional rule: the gamemaster may add about +5 to the difficulty (as low as +1 for simple tasks); some tasks are impossible untrained. No untrained modifier when the text gives the attribute directly (resisting wounds), most dodge/brawling in combat, search for clues, or willpower against interaction and Force attacks. (p.75)

sections.title: Large dice pools
sections.text: Optional. Fast: roll 5 dice (incl. wild die), add the pips and a bonus by die code. Faster: roll only the wild die, add pips and a bonus. Character Point dice are rolled separately. With a Force Point, double the original die code before the lookup. Beyond 50D: 5-dice bonus = ceil((D-5) x 3.5); wild-die bonus = ceil((D-1) x 3.5). Table: `tables/die-code-simplification.json`. (p.75)

sections.title: Scenes and rounds
sections.text:
- **Scene**: ordinary time; the gamemaster narrates, players act, rolls only when needed. Can span minutes to weeks. (p.77)
- **Round**: 5 seconds; used when every second matters (combat, chases, deadlines). Each round = Initiative, then Roll Actions. (p.77)

sections.title: Initiative
sections.text:
1. The highest-Perception character on each side rolls Perception; the winner chooses whether their side acts first or last that round. Reroll ties. (p.78)
2. Initiative is not an action. Character Points and Force Points **cannot** be used on it; wound penalties still apply. (p.78)
3. Tie-break order: ability/talent that goes first; Perception; search; Dexterity; dodge; special equipment or situation. (p.78)

sections.title: Rolling actions
sections.text:
- The acting side goes in Perception order (highest first). Each player declares how many actions they will take this round, then rolls the first one. (p.78)
- After everyone has taken a first action, sides take second actions, and so on. Actions cannot be skipped to act later. (p.78)
- A Force Point or Character Points may be declared at any time, but **not both in the same round**. (p.78)

sections.title: Multiple actions
sections.text:
- Each action beyond the first gives **-1D to all skill and attribute rolls** that round (not damage, damage resistance or initiative). Four actions = -3D on every roll. (p.78)
- A special ability that raises the base number of actions delays the penalty until the allotment is used. (p.78)
- Only weapons and equipment suited to quick use can be used several times in a round. A skill or attribute reduced to 0 cannot be used. (p.78)

sections.title: Reaction skills
sections.text:
- Acrobatics, dodge, melee parry and brawling parry are used when attacked; the player may wait until attacked. (p.79)
- The reaction uses up a remaining action, **or** is taken as an extra action (raising the multiple-action penalty for the rest of the round). (p.79)
- The reaction roll **replaces** the attacker's original difficulty number for the rest of the round, even if lower or higher. (p.79) Details: Combat chapter.

sections.title: Free actions and non-roll actions
sections.text:
- **Free actions** need no roll and no real effort: initiative roll, a sentence or two of speech, a quick look around, grabbing something simple, cautious movement in Easy/Very Easy/Moderate terrain, Strength roll to resist damage (always full Strength even when wounded), control/Perception roll to resist Force or mental powers (full dice). (p.80)
- **Non-roll actions** count as an action (so they cost -1D on other rolls) but need no roll: reloading, basic datapad lookup, very slow piloting, anything needing concentration. (p.81)
- The book lists actions that take time in a round (bash, catch, choke, communicate, disarm, dodge, entangle, escape, grab, kick, leap, lunge, move, parry, pin, punch, push, ready a weapon, run away, shoot, slash, switch setting, tackle, throw, trip, use a skill, vehicle maneuver) with a suggested skill each. (p.80-81) Full list with the suggested skills: `raw-data/05-the-rules.txt`, section "Actions That Take Time" (printed p.80-81).

sections.title: How long things take
sections.text:
- Each skill lists a "time taken". One-round skills can be repeated in a round if suited (blaster); some one-round skills (first aid, computer programming/repair, piloting a landspeeder) absorb the whole round. (p.81)
- **Preparing**: spend twice the time for **+1D** per doubling, max **+3D**; nothing else can be done meanwhile. Not for dodges, parries or piloting skills; rarely for survival, hide, stamina, swimming. Aiming a blaster an extra round is a typical use. (p.82)
- **Rushing**: only for tasks that take two rounds or more. Do it in half the time but roll **half** the skill dice. Gamemaster decides if allowed. (p.82)
- **Multiple-roll tasks**: the gamemaster may split a hard task into several easier rolls. (p.81-82)

sections.title: Combined actions
sections.text:
Several characters cooperating on one task. (p.83-84)
1. All must agree. While combining they can only roll reaction skills.
2. The leader is the character with the highest **command** (or Perception). Leader can command at most as many characters as they have command/Perception dice.
3. Leader rolls command against a gamemaster-set difficulty (task complexity, precision, group size, skill, familiarity, time). If supervising only, full command; if also working, it counts as two actions (-1D).
4. Success: bonus = **+1D per 3 characters**, +1 per one extra, +2 per two extra (8 characters = +2D+2).
5. Failure: reduce the bonus by **1D for each point missed** (minimum 0). Example in book: bonus +2D+2, difficulty 12; roll 11 -> +1D+2; roll 10 -> +2; roll 9 or less -> none.
6. The bonus goes to the highest-skilled character doing the task. In combat it can be split between attack and damage; multi-roll tasks can split it across rolls.

sections.title: Character Points
sections.text:
- No limit on how many a character holds. Spend to add **1 extra die per point** to a skill or attribute roll; the die explodes on a 6 like a wild die. (p.84)
- May be spent after the roll, before anyone else acts. **Not in the same round or scene as a Force Point or calling on the dark side.** (p.84)
- Limits per roll: 2 for a skill/attribute roll; 2 for attack damage; 5 for specialization; 5 for acrobatics/dodge/parries (incl. lightsaber parries and vehicle dodges); 5 for Strength to resist damage. Never on another character's actions. (p.85) Data: `tables/character-force-point-limits.json`.
- In scenes, only for one continuous action. (p.85)
- They also buy permanent skill improvement (see Characters chapter).

sections.title: Force Points
sections.text:
- Spending one in a round **doubles all skill, attribute and special-ability die codes** for the rest of that round. Things that are not the character (weapon damage dice, hull codes) are not doubled. (p.85)
- Melee damage: double the user's Strength dice, not the weapon bonus. (STR 3D+2, vibro-ax STR+2D -> 6D+4 + 2D.) (p.85)
- One per round. Non-Force-sensitive characters can hold at most 5; Force-sensitive characters have no cap. All player characters start with at least 1. (p.85)
- In scenes, only for one continuous action. Not usable in the same round/scene as Character Points. (p.85)
- **End of adventure**: evil use = lose it permanently **and** gain a Dark Side Point; unheroic use = lose it permanently; heroic use = get it back; heroic at a dramatically appropriate moment = get it back **plus one more**. A character with none can earn one by being heroic at such a moment. (p.86)
- Examples of evil, unheroic and heroic uses are listed on p.86.

sections.title: Dark Side Points
sections.text:
- The gamemaster should warn the player before an action that would give a Dark Side Point. (p.86)
- When one is gained, roll 1D: if the roll is **less than** the total Dark Side Points, the character has turned to the dark side. (p.86) 6 Dark Side Points means fallen. (p.87)
- **Atonement**: possible with 1-5 points; must follow the Jedi code strictly and actively prevent evil; generally two adventures (or 40 game days) to remove one point, at the gamemaster's judgment. (p.87)
- **Calling upon the dark side** (anyone, Force-sensitive or not): you automatically gain a Dark Side Point whether or not it works. Roll control or Perception against Easy (Force-sensitive) or Moderate (not); +2 difficulty levels if no harm is intended; **+3** per additional use in the same adventure. Success grants a Force Point to be spent immediately, in addition to others that round. Failure: roll 1D and lose that many Character Points, or lose 1D from an attribute or Force skill (player chooses); reduced to 0D means consumed by the dark side and death. Not available to characters who deny the Force. (p.87)

sections.title: Quick reference
sections.text:
| Situation | Rule |
|---|---|
| Succeed | roll >= difficulty |
| Tie, opposed | initiator wins |
| Extra action | -1D to every roll that round |
| Force Point | double character dice for the round |
| Character Point | +1D (exploding) after the roll |
| FP and CP same round | not allowed |
| Prepare | +1D per doubling of time, max +3D |
| Rush | half time, half dice |

sections.title: Equipment, weapons and armor (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. Items are in `weapons.json` (63 items), `armor.json` (15) and `gear.json` (54); prices, codes and licenses are in `tables/equipment-tables.json`. Each item record keeps the book's fields (`model`, `type`, `scale`, `skill`, `cost`, `availability`, `difficulty`, `damage`, `range`, `ammo`, `fire_rate`, `blast_radius`, `game_notes`...) plus `cost_credits` (null when not for sale) and `page`.

sections.title: Availability and restrictions
sections.text: (p.334) Availability **1** readily available everywhere; **2** large cities, spaceports or the item's home planet; **3** specialized, normally only on its home planet; **4** rare, hard to obtain. Restriction codes: **F** fee or permit often required, **R** restricted (cannot normally be sold without a license), **X** illegal on most planets.

sections.title: Licenses
sections.text: Pay a fee (a percentage of the item's base cost, in addition to the item) then roll bureaucracy or a Knowledge skill: **Fee/Permit 5%, Moderate, 1 day; Restricted 10%, Difficult, 1D days; Military/Illegal 50%, Very Difficult, 2D days.** Success grants the license after that time; failure costs the time and the fee, and you may retry. Bribery uses persuasion, a false or stolen identity uses forgery; failing by 5 or more alerts the authorities. Every application leaves a record. (p.334) Most restricted items can be found on the black market for effort and money.

sections.title: Buying and selling
sections.text: Listed costs are averages; the gamemaster may vary them. A merchant generally buys used equipment at **half** its listed price (commodities excluded). Commodity prices, services and expenses (meals, lodging, medical treatment, passage, rentals, upkeep) are in `tables/equipment-tables.json`. (p.334-335, p.359)

sections.title: Weapons
sections.text:
(p.346-356) Records in `weapons.json`; `category` is one of melee, archaic-ranged, blaster, miscellaneous, artillery or explosive. How to use the fields in combat: `combat-injuries.md` (range bands from the three range numbers, fire rate, ammo, blast radius, stun settings, scale).
- **Damage**: a die code (`4D`), `STR+1D` for melee (roll Strength plus the dice; a `maximum` caps it), or blast bands such as `5D/4D/3D/2D` with a matching `blast_radius`.
- **Skill**: the skill and specialization used (for example "Blaster: blaster pistol"); an unimproved skill uses its attribute.
- **Difficulty**: melee weapons carry their own difficulty to use; ranged weapons use the range bands instead.
- Explosive accessories (detonators, fuses) have no damage and are flagged `accessory`.

- **Melee (18)**: Amphistaff, Atlatl, Bayonet, Cesta, Club, Electrostaff, Force Pike, Gaderffii Stick, Hatchet, Knife, Spear, Staff, Stun Gauntlets, Vibro-Ax, Vibroblade, Lightsaber, Double-Bladed Lightsaber, Short Lightsaber.

sections.title: Armor
sections.text:
(p.356-358) Armor adds its die code to the **Strength roll to resist damage** for the covered body location (head, torso, left/right arm, left/right leg; front and back may differ). `armor.json` has `protection` parsed from the notes (`physical`, `energy`, `dexterity_penalty`), but read `game_notes` for coverage, helmet systems and special equipment (comlink, MFTAS, utility belts). Rules for armor damage and how it interacts with attacks: `combat-injuries.md#armor`.

sections.title: Cybernetics
sections.text: (p.341-342) Replacement prosthetics duplicate the natural part (1 cyber point each) at fixed prices; enhancements raise an attribute and its improved skills at cost `base x pips x starting die code` and add Dark Side Points (+1 per transgression for 1-2 enhancements, +2 for 3-4, +3 for 5-6). A replacement counts as half an enhancement for that purpose. Optional: cyber points reduce Force skills. Details and examples: `tables/equipment-tables.json` (`cybernetics`). The book says cybernetics are not a shopping list for player characters.

sections.title: The Force (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. All 77 powers (skills, difficulty text, prerequisites, time, warning, first-sentence summary, page) are in `force-powers.json`; for full effects and examples open the raw chapter at the power's page. Other numbers: `tables/force.json`.

sections.title: Who can use the Force
sections.text: Only **Force-sensitive** characters learn Force skills and powers (see `characters.md#force-sensitivity`). Several templates start with them (alien student of the Force, failed Jedi, minor Jedi, quixotic Jedi, young Jedi). Everyone else must find a teacher. (p.150)

sections.title: The Jedi Code (summary)
sections.text: (p.149) Peace over emotion, knowledge over ignorance, serenity over passion, the Force over death. The Jedi preserves life; killing is permitted only in self-defense or defense of others and is still a stain. Act calm, never from fear, hatred or anger. Seek nonviolent solutions first. Use Force powers responsibly, for the light, **never for personal gain, power or convenience**. Do not allow evil by inaction, and do not associate with those who willfully do evil. Each use of the Force sends a tremor that others can detect; frequent use makes you easy to find.

sections.title: Force skills
sections.text:
Three skills: **control** (your own body), **sense** (the world and others), **alter** (changing the Force and things). (p.151)
- **First learning**: a teacher with at least 3D (higher than your skill) and Force-sensitivity; **10 Character Points**, one week (a day less per extra point, minimum one day). You start at **1D** and are taught one power of that skill. Control is usually taught first, alter last. (p.151)
- **Improving**: cost per pip = the number before the "D" (double without a teacher); training 1 day per point with a teacher, 2 without. (p.151)
- **Teaching others**: needs 3D in the skill and the power known; teaching someone with Dark Side Points gives the teacher a Dark Side Point. (p.150-151)

sections.title: Learning powers
sections.text: (p.152) A power must be taught. One power on first learning a skill; **one new power per pip** of Force skill improvement (chosen by the teacher, using the improved skill); or **5 Character Points** for a power without improving a skill. A power using two skills counts as **two** powers, three skills as **three**. You must already know the **Required Powers**. Optional: willpower against a learning difficulty (5 + 5 per prerequisite) instead of prerequisites. (p.175)

sections.title: Using powers
sections.text:
(p.152-153)
- Each Force skill a power needs is a **separate action**. Roll them in consecutive rounds at full dice, or all in one round with the multiple-action penalty (two skills: -1D each).
- Each power lists a difficulty per skill; the gamemaster may add modifiers. The target may resist with control or Perception where stated.
- **Relationship** adds to difficulty: close relatives +0, close friends +2, friends +5, acquaintances +7, slight acquaintances +10, met once +12, known by reputation +15, strangers +20, strangers of another species +30.
- **Proximity** adds: touching +0, line of sight +2, out of sight 1-100 m +5, 101 m-10 km +7, 11-1,000 km +10, same planet farther +15, same system +20, other system +30.
- **Keeping a power "up"** (only if the entry says so; announce it when activating): no new rolls each round, but you lose dice as if taking actions (-1D per Force skill the power uses; lightsaber combat -2D). Stunned, wounded or worse drops every "up" power. Otherwise a power ends at the end of the round (some, like combat sense, have their own duration).
- No Time to Use listed = one round. **Warning** powers give a Dark Side Point on every use.
- **Stretching a power** beyond its text is up to the gamemaster (a modest stretch +1 or 2 levels).
