sections.text:
- **Control (20)**: Absorb/Dissipate Energy, Accelerate Healing, Burst of Speed, Concentration, Contort/Escape, Control Disease, Control Pain, Detoxify Poison, Emptiness, Enhance Attribute, Force of Will, Hibernation Trance, Instinctive Astrogation Control, Rage, Reduce Injury, Remain Conscious, Remove Fatigue, Resist Stun, Short-Term Memory Enhancement, Up the Walls.
- **Sense (19)**: Beast Languages, Combat Sense, Danger Sense, Direction Sense, Instinctive Astrogation, Life Detection, Life Sense, Life Web, Magnify Senses, Merge Senses, Postcognition, Predict Natural Disaster, Receptive Telepathy, Sense Force, Sense Force Potential, Sense Path, Shift Sense, Translation, Weather Sense.
- **Alter (4)**: Force Push, Injure/Kill, Kinetic Combat, Telekinesis.
- **Control and sense (5)**: Farseeing, Life Bond, Lifemerge, Lightsaber Combat, Projective Telepathy.
- **Control and alter (14)**: Accelerate Another's Healing, Control Another's Disease, Control Another's Pain, Control Breathing, Detoxify Another's Poison, Feed on Dark Side, Force Jump, Force Lightning, Inflict Pain, Place Another in Hibernation Trance, Redirect Energy, Remove Another's Fatigue, Return Another to Consciousness, Transfer Force.

Query examples:
```

jq '.powers[] | select(.warning) | .name' data/force-powers.json
```

sections.title: The dark side
sections.text:
(p.152, p.177-178; basic rules in `core-mechanics.md#dark-side`)
- **Bonus**: with Dark Side Points you add **+1D per point** to Force skill rolls. You may refuse it, but then every Force power's difficulty rises at least one level. A fallen character no longer gets it. (p.152)
- **Gaining points**: by **action** (knowingly breaking the Jedi Code, hate- or anger-fueled violence, evil acts, dark side powers, a Force Point used for evil), **inaction** (standing by while evil is done) or **calling upon the dark side**. (p.177)
- **Falling**: normally a character with more than six points becomes a gamemaster character; optional rules allow continuing play (no normal Character Points, only one per Dark Side Point gained). (p.177; see E-044)
- **Returning to the light**: spend a Force Point selflessly at a dramatically appropriate moment (usually a heroic sacrifice). Cost: all Force Points and Character Points; Dark Side Points drop to **5**. (p.178)
- **Atonement** (1-5 points): act to preserve life, knowledge, peace and the defenseless, non-violently where possible. Time to remove: **40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 days** for 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 points; restart if a new point is gained. (p.178)

sections.title: Movement and chases (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. Starship movement and combat is a separate chapter (`space.md`, planned).

sections.title: Character movement
sections.text:
(p.107-108) Data: `tables/movement.json`.
- Every character has a **Move** (meters per round walking; humans usually 10). Moving is **one action per round**. Roll **running** (or Dexterity); swimming uses swimming/Strength and climbing uses climbing/jumping/Strength, normally at **one-third** Move.
- Terrain gives a difficulty level (Very Easy 1-5 ... Heroic 31+); the gamemaster picks the number. Roll >= it or have a **movement failure**.
- Four speeds (pick one per round):

| Speed | Distance | Very Easy / Easy / Moderate terrain | Difficult / Very Difficult / Heroic terrain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cautious | Move x 1/2 | **free action**, no roll | roll, difficulty **-1 level** |
| Cruising | Move x 1 | an action, automatic | roll |
| High speed | Move x 2 | roll | difficulty **+1 level** (Heroic becomes Heroic +10) |
| All-out | Move x 4 | roll, difficulty **+1 level**; do nothing else (no dodge or parry) | roll, difficulty **+2 levels** |

- **Partial moves**: between half and the full distance of the chosen speed.
- **Acceleration**: characters change speed **up to two levels per round**; vehicles one level (E-034).

sections.title: Encumbrance (optional)
sections.text: One medium-sized object per **pip** of Strength (3D+2 = 11). Over that, apply long-distance movement and stamina. (p.108)

sections.title: Long-distance movement
sections.text: (p.109) Stamina roll every **minute** at all-out and every **10 minutes** at high speed (first Very Easy, +1 level each roll); on failure rest twice as long as you moved. Marching at cruising speed: Very Easy stamina check every 3 hours (every 2 if continuous), +1 level each; one hour of sleep per check made restores vigor.

sections.title: Movement failures
sections.text:
(p.109-110) Margin = difficulty - roll.

| Missed by | Result |
|---|---|
| 1-3 | Slight slip: -1D to all actions for the rest of the round |
| 4-6 | Slip: half Move; -3D rest of round, -1D next round |
| 7-10 | Fall: halfway, kneeling; no actions this round; -2D next round |
| 11-15 | Minor tumble: no actions this and next round; collision damage -3D |
| 16-20 | Tumble: normal collision damage |
| 21+ | Major tumble: collision damage +2D |

Collision damage: cautious 1D, cruise 2D, high 3D, all-out 4D, rolled against Strength (`combat-injuries.md#damage`).

sections.title: Vehicle movement
sections.text:
(p.110-112) Data: `tables/vehicle-movement-damage.json`.
- A vehicle's **Move** is its cruising distance per round. Pilot rolls the vehicle's operation skill (repulsorlift operation for most speeders; walker, ground vehicle, hover vehicle or swoop operation otherwise; Mechanical if unskilled) **plus the vehicle's maneuverability code**.
- Same four speeds and terrain shifts as characters (cautious is free in easy terrain; all-out x4, no other action, no vehicle dodges or weapons).
- Vehicles accelerate or decelerate **one level per round**; partial moves between half and full.
- Long distance: body strength roll every 10 minutes at all-out and every hour at high speed (first Very Easy, +1 level each); failure by 1-10 means strain and rest, by 11+ a mechanical failure (Moderate repair roll, at least an hour).
- **Terrain examples and maneuver modifiers** (bootlegger turn, extreme climb/dive/turn, jump, loop, rotate) are in the data file. (p.111-112)

sections.title: Vehicle movement failures
sections.text:
| Missed by | Result |
|---|---|
| 1-3 | Slight slip: pilot -1D rest of round |
| 4-6 | Slip: half Move; pilot -3D this round, -1D next |
| 7-10 | Spin: a quarter of its Move, no movement this and next round |
| 11-15 | Minor collision: collision damage -3D (or spin if nothing to hit) |
| 16-20 | Collision: normal collision damage |
| 21+ | Major collision: collision damage +4D |

**Collision damage** by speed: cautious 2D, cruise 4D, high 6D, all-out 10D. Angle against another vehicle: head-on **+3D**, rear-end/sideswipe **-3D**, T-bone 0D. Soft obstacles may reduce it by -1D or more. Roll against the vehicle's body strength. (p.113)

sections.title: Vehicle combat
sections.text:
(p.113-115)
- Same as regular combat: difficulty by range, roll vehicle blasters (or Dexterity) **plus fire control**, >= difficulty hits. All Combat chapter modifiers, scale and cover (None, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, Full) apply.
- **Vehicle dodge**: pilot's operation skill + maneuverability becomes the new difficulty. **Full vehicle dodge**: only action of the round (not even moving); the roll is **added** to every attack's difficulty (example: 25 turns difficulty 12 into 37). (p.113)
- **Weapon ranges**: with four ranges, the first is point-blank (Very Easy); closer than that is Very Difficult. **Crew** N means N gunners are needed but only one rolls. **Fire arcs**: front, back, left, right, turret. (p.114-115)
- **Ramming**: pass close to the target; difficulty **+10** and a separate action (extra -1D). Roll above the new difficulty: the ram hits; below the original: movement failure; in between: you complete the move but miss. The attacker takes sideswipe damage (-3D), the victim T-bone (normal). The target may vehicle dodge. (p.115; E-033 for the tie case)
- **Complex maneuvers**: Attack Pattern Delta (each pilot Easy repulsorlift operation to form up; followers +1D against attackers dead ahead) and Bantha Decoy (opposed tactics or Perception for the walker's commander; if fooled, +1D+2 to the trailing speeder and +5 difficulty for the walker's gunners). (p.114)

sections.title: Vehicle damage
sections.text:
(p.115-116) Damage roll vs body strength roll: lower = none. Margin **0-3** shields blown or controls ionized, **4-8** lightly, **9-12** heavily, **13-15** severely damaged, **16+** destroyed.
- **Shields blown**: -1D shields (if none, controls ionized). **Controls ionized**: -1D to maneuverability, fire control, weapon damage and shields for this round and the next; as many ionized results as maneuverability dice freezes the controls for two rounds.
- **Lightly / heavily / severely damaged** roll 1D for the system hit (tables in the data file); repeating a worse state escalates it. **Lost Moves** add up: -1 no all-out, -2 cruising max, -3 cautious only, -4 immobile, -5 destroyed.
- **Passengers** (character-scale damage, gamemaster's judgment): lightly 1D, heavily 3D, severely 6D, destroyed 12D.
- **Falling**: damage matches the faller's scale; same distance table as characters (`damage-healing.json`).

sections.title: Speeds in kilometers per hour
sections.text: (p.117) All-out km/h = Move x 2.88 (rounded table in `tables/speed-conversion.json`). High speed = half of that, cruising = one quarter, cautious = one eighth. Example: Move 350 -> 1,000 / 500 / 250 / 125 km/h.

sections.title: Attributes and skills (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are the book's printed pages. The per-skill list is in `skills.json` (110 skills: attribute, time taken, specializations, summary, page, advanced prerequisites). For difficulty tables and examples of a given skill, open `raw-data/03-attributes-skills.txt` at the page given in `skills.json`.

sections.title: The one rule
sections.text: The gamemaster picks a difficulty number; if the roll is **equal or higher**, the character succeeds. (p.33) See `core-mechanics.md#difficulty`.

sections.title: Attributes
sections.text:
Six attributes: **Dexterity, Knowledge, Mechanical, Perception, Strength, Technical**. Each covers many skills; an unimproved skill uses its attribute's die code. (p.32)

| Attribute | Skills in `skills.json` |
|---|---|
| Dexterity | 20 (combat, reactions, running, pick pocket) |
| Knowledge | 14 |
| Mechanical | 23 (vehicle and starship operation, sensors, communications) |
| Perception | 10 |
| Strength | 5 (brawling, climbing/jumping, lifting, stamina, swimming) |
| Technical | 21 plus 17 advanced (A) skills (repair, programming, engineering, medicine) |

sections.title: How a skill entry reads
sections.text:
- **Time Taken**: how long using the skill generally takes (one round, minutes, hours, days). A guideline; the gamemaster can change it. Many combat skills can be used in one round (so they can be repeated with the multiple-action penalty). (p.33)
- **Specializations**: examples of narrower focuses (see `characters.md#pick-skills` for cost and use). Some skills list none.
- **Advanced skills** are marked `(A)` (`advanced: true` in the data), start at 1D, need prerequisite skills and cost double to improve. `prerequisites_text` holds the requirement; the engineering list is on p.62-63.

sections.title: Ranged combat skills (p.33)
sections.text:
Archaic guns, artillery, blaster, blaster artillery, bowcaster, bows, firearms, flamethrower, grenade, missile weapons, thrown weapons, vehicle blasters. Starship gunnery and capital ship gunnery are also ranged combat skills but belong to Mechanical.
- Difficulty depends on **range**: farther = harder (each weapon lists its ranges; see the equipment chapter).
- Roll >= difficulty hits, but the target may use a reaction skill or have cover (see `combat-injuries.md`, planned).
- Use the right skill for the weapon: for example, `blaster` covers hand-held character-scale blasters, not fixed or multi-crew weapons (blaster artillery), vehicle-mounted weapons (vehicle blasters) or starship weapons (starship/capital ship gunnery). (p.35)

sections.title: Melee combat skills (p.33)
sections.text:
Melee combat and lightsaber; brawling (Strength) is also a melee combat skill. Each melee weapon has its own difficulty number; roll >= it to hit; the target may parry or have cover.
- **Lightsaber danger** (p.36): if an attacker misses the difficulty by **10 or more**, they hurt themselves and roll the weapon's damage against their own Strength. (The book's example: difficulty 20, roll of 10 or lower, 5D self-damage.)

sections.title: Reaction skills (p.33)
sections.text:
Acrobatics, brawling parry, dodge, melee parry; lightsaber can also parry (brawling, lightsaber and melee attacks; parrying blaster bolts needs the lightsaber combat Force power). Mechanical vehicle and starship skills can be used for **vehicle dodges**.
- Which reaction against what: **dodge** = any ranged attack; **melee parry** = melee, brawling or lightsaber attacks when you hold a melee weapon (not blasters); **brawling parry** = brawling or melee attacks while unarmed. (p.36)
- When attacked, the reaction roll **becomes** the attacker's difficulty number. (p.33; see `core-mechanics.md#reactions`)
- **Full reaction** (p.33): roll the reaction skill and **add** the roll to the attackers' difficulty numbers; the character **cannot do anything else** that round.
- The reaction-skill Character Point cap is 5 (see `core-mechanics.md#character-points`).

sections.title: Acrobatics
sections.text:
(p.33-35) One round; specializations: type of acrobatics (diving, trapeze, tumbling).
- Tumble, leap and roll to avoid falling damage, entertain, or surprise an opponent.
- **Boosting other skills**: the gamemaster sets the stunt's difficulty; **half the difference (rounded up)** between the difficulty and the acrobatics roll is added to the complementary climbing/jumping or running roll. Both must be done on the same turn, so the multiple-action penalty applies. The same bonus can be added to an intimidation attempt, on the same turn or the next round.
- Instead of raising a running or swimming difficulty for an obstacle course, the gamemaster may ask for an acrobatics roll in addition.
- During a fall, acrobatics may reduce damage if the character still has declared actions to spend this round.
- Combined maneuvers: use the hardest maneuver's difficulty and **+5** for each additional maneuver.
- Difficulty examples (p.35): Very Easy somersault or pirouette; Easy handspring, cartwheel, handstand; Moderate round-off, back-flip, vaulting an obstacle; Very Difficult bouncing off a surface to a specific destination. Modifiers to the difficulty: -3 unlimited landing area; +3 limited, rough or unsteady landing area, high to low surface, slippery or strong wind; +6 almost no landing area, low to high surface, or narrow surface. Penalties to the roll: -3 or more per twist, backwards or underwater; -9 or more in the air (trapeze, bars).

sections.text:
```
jq '.skills[] | select(.attribute=="dexterity") | {name, time_taken, specializations, page}' data/skills.json
jq '.skills[] | select(.advanced) | {name, prerequisites_text}' data/skills.json
```

sections.title: Space travel and combat (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. Ship statistics (hull, shields, Space, maneuverability, weapons) are in the Starships chapter (`starships.json`, planned).

sections.title: Starships
sections.text:
- **Capital ship**: big combat vessels; skill **capital ship piloting**. **Starfighter**: small combat craft; **starfighter piloting**. **Space transport**: everything else (freighters, shuttles, yachts, liners); **space transports**. (p.120) The text says each can fall back on the Technical attribute, but these skills are Mechanical (E-036).
- All starship combat happens in realspace at sublight speeds. Sublight benchmarks (orbit to jump point 5 min, planet to moon 30 min, planet to planet 2-6 hours) are in the data file. (p.121)

sections.title: Hyperspace
sections.text:
(p.121-125) Data: `tables/space-travel.json`.
- **Hyperdrive class** is a multiplier on a route's standard duration (x1 = standard; x2 takes twice as long; x0.5 half). Backup drives are x10 or worse. (p.122)
- **Making a jump** (astrogation):
  1. The gamemaster sets a difficulty (most trips Moderate), modified by: **no nav computer or astromech +30**; **hasty entry x2** (one-round jump instead of one minute); lightly damaged ship +5, heavily damaged +10; **-1 per extra hour** added to the trip, **+1 per hour saved**; obstacles +1 to +30. (p.123)
  2. Calculation time: 1 minute on a well-known route or with precalculated coordinates; about half an hour between known systems; a few hours for a new system; 1 day if lost.
  3. Roll astrogation: **>= difficulty** and the jump works; **miss by 1-9** an astrogation mishap (2D table); **miss by 10+** no jump, roll again.
- **Mishaps** (2D, p.124): 2 hyperdrive cut-out and damaged; 3-4 radiation fluctuations (+/-1D hours per point missed); 5-6 cut-out into realspace; 7-8 off course; 9 mynocks (+1D days); 10 close call (a system damaged); 11-12 collision, heavy damage, ship abandoned (survival and stamina rolls for a hull rupture).
- **Stopping a jump**: damage adds to the astrogation difficulty (+5 light, +10 heavy), each ion-cannon controls ionized result +5, a tractor beam adds its damage roll; hasty jumps double the base. All cumulative. (p.125)

sections.title: Sensors and communications
sections.text: (p.126-127) Operator rolls **sensors**; the difficulty depends on range and conditions. Four modes: **passive**, **scan** (all directions), **search** (one fire arc), **focus** (small area). Each is listed `range in Space units / dice added to sensors` (e.g. Scan 25/1D). Countermeasures: hide behind a planet, go passive, run silent (about five minutes max), jam, decoys, sensor masks, false transponder codes. Comms and subspace work only in realspace.

sections.title: Licenses and starport costs
sections.text: (p.128-130) Operating license 1,000 credits; captain's license 300 (500 with the expediter fee); arms load-out permit from 250 per weapon or boosted shield system. Docking about 50 credits per day (up to 150 at busy Imperial/Republic ports); restocking = base fee (about 10, up to 35) x crew and passengers x days; overhaul every 20 jumps about 1,000 credits (up to 5,000); traffic fines 50-200 credits.

sections.title: Starship movement
sections.text:
(p.131-134) Data: `tables/starship-combat.json` (`movement`). Same structure as vehicles in `movement-chases.md#vehicle-movement`, with **Space units** instead of meters.
- A ship has a **Space** score (cruising distance per round; slow 2-3, freighters 5-6, fastest fighters 11-12). Pilot rolls the piloting skill **plus maneuverability**; >= difficulty or a movement failure.
- Speeds: cautious (half, round up; free action in Very Easy/Easy/Moderate space), cruising, high (x2; harder space +1 level), all-out (x4; no other action; +1 level easy space, +2 levels hard space). One level of acceleration per round. Partial moves between half and full.
- Long distance: **hull code** roll every 10 minutes at all-out and every hour at high speed.
- Failures by margin: 1-3 slight slip (-1D), 4-6 slip (half move, -3D then -1D), 7-10 spin, 11-15 minor collision (-3D damage), 16-20 collision, 21+ major collision (+4D); with nothing to hit the ship spins out of control for this round and the next.
- Collisions: cautious 2D, cruise 4D, high 6D, all-out 10D; head-on +3D, sideswipe or rear-end -3D, T-bone 0D.

sections.title: Starship combat
sections.text:
(p.134-137)
- Same flow as combat: difficulty by the weapon's range in **Space units**, roll **starship gunnery** (starfighter scale) or **capital ship gunnery** (capital scale) **plus fire control**; >= difficulty hits. Every starship gives full cover.
- **Starship dodge**: piloting skill + maneuverability becomes the new difficulty. **Full starship dodge**: only action of the round; the roll is **added** to all attacks' difficulties.
- **Fire-linked weapons**: stats are for the linked group; firing separately reduces damage by the combined-action bonus (four lasers 6D together, each 4D+1 alone).
- **Ion cannons** ignore shields; damage over the hull code roll by 0-3 / 4-8 / 9-12 / 13-15 / 16+ gives 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 controls ionized / controls dead.
- **Missiles, bombs, proton torpedoes**: difficulty +5 / +10 / +15 / +20 against targets with Space 3 / 4 / 5 / 6+.
- **Tractor beams**: a hit, then beam damage against hull code; a captured ship that does not resist is reeled in 5 units per round; resisting, a beam roll equal or higher reels in 1-4 units and costs the target -1 to -4 Move.
- **Called shots on ships** (higher scale cannot target a lower scale's parts): primary section +2D, subsection +4D, specific location +8D. (p.136)
- **Optional power control** (p.137): reroute up to +2D to a system; difficulty Moderate / Difficult / Very Difficult by complexity; time by the operator's roll.

sections.title: Shields
sections.text: (p.134-135) Using shields is a **reaction skill** (starship shields; capital ship shields for capital ships). Split the shield dice among the four fire arcs; difficulty is **Easy / Moderate / Difficult / Very Difficult** for 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 arcs. Hits from a covered arc add the shield dice to the **hull code** to resist damage. Particle shields must be dropped to launch fighters, missiles or torpedoes (hull code -2D).

sections.title: Starship damage
sections.text:
(p.137-139) Roll damage against the **hull code roll**; lower = no damage. Margin **0-3** shields blown or controls ionized, **4-8** lightly, **9-12** heavily, **13-15** severely damaged, **16+** destroyed.
- **Controls ionized**: -1D to maneuverability, shields, fire control and weapon damage for this round and the next; as many results as maneuverability dice freeze the controls for two rounds.
- Lightly, heavily and severely damaged each roll 1D on a system table (maneuverability, weapons, hyperdrive, shields, Move, drives, generator...) in the data file; repeating a worse state escalates it. **Lost Moves** add up: -1 no all-out, -2 cruising max, -3 cautious only, -4 dead in space, -5 destroyed.
- A **hyperdrive hit** doubles calculation times (light) or adds +10 to astrogation (heavy), fixed by one hour and a Moderate repair roll.

sections.title: Species (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. Full stat blocks (attribute ranges, special skills, special abilities, story factors, Move, size) for all 47 entries are in `species.json`; each entry's `page` points to the book page.

sections.title: How to read an entry
sections.text:
(p.278)
- **Attribute Dice**: dice for an average member of the species. **Player characters and some gamemaster characters get 6D more** (`characters.md#new-template`).
- **Attribute die ranges**: each attribute has `minimum/maximum`. Members cannot go below the minimum or above the maximum at creation (with a few exceptions); Character Points can later raise attributes above the maximum (the ceiling check in `characters.md#advancement`).
- **Special skills**: skills common to the species, each tied to an attribute; anyone can learn them with instruction.
- **Special abilities**: physiological traits (claws, tails, natural armor, vision...) that others cannot learn. Some matter only at character creation (skill bonuses and limits); write down those that matter in play.
- **Story factors**: culture, life cycle and prejudices that affect most members; roleplaying and gamemaster hooks.
- **Move**: `start/maximum`; a character starts with the first number and can raise it to the second (`characters.md#advancement`). Species with several movement modes list each.
- **Size**: usual adult height.
- **Languages**: everyone can speak Basic; a nonhuman also has their species language as a specialization at **5D** (for example language: Cerean 5D), which does not raise the general languages skill. (p.278)

sections.title: Era restrictions
sections.text: (p.280) Old Republic / Rise of the Empire / Dark Times: all species available except ones not yet discovered (no Ewoks). Rebellion: most aliens are enslaved or second-class under the Empire, free Wookiees are rare, Ewoks appear only late. New Republic: aliens regain equal standing. New Jedi Order and later: all species available.

sections.title: Humans, near-humans and clones
sections.text:
- **Humans**: 12D, every attribute **2D/4D**, Move **10/12**, 1.5-2.0 m, no special abilities. (p.279)
- **Near-humans** usually share human stats, but some races have different ranges or minor abilities. (p.279)
- **Republic Clone** (for player characters and major gamemaster characters): fixed values (Dexterity 3D, Knowledge 2D+1, Mechanical 2D+2, Perception 2D+1, Strength 3D, Technical 2D+1) with **+2D** to add, **no more than 2 pips per attribute**; Military Training (extra 2D for military skills at creation), Obedient and Accelerated Growth story factors; Move 10/12. (p.279)

sections.title: How a template is used
sections.text:
1. Start from the attribute codes (the template's total is in `attribute_total`).
2. Put **7D** of beginning skill dice into the skills listed on the template (1D or 2D each; more skills only with the gamemaster's permission); unimproved skills use the attribute (`characters.md#pick-skills`).
3. Decide Force sensitivity where the template leaves it blank: yes = 2 Force Points, no = 1. Templates that begin with Force skills must be Force-sensitive and choose Force powers (`force.md`).
4. Equipment and credits come from the template; every character starts with 5 Character Points.
5. Droids use the Droids chapter's rules (the Protocol Droid template is the exception: 17D to allocate, not more than 2D per skill).

sections.title: Vehicles and starships (player view)
sections.text: Page numbers `(p.N)` are printed pages. Vehicle rules are in `movement-chases.md`, starship rules in `space.md`; this file explains the statistics and lists what is in the data files. Records keep the book's labelled fields (`craft`, `type`, `scale`, `skill`, `crew`, `crew_skill`, `passengers`, `cargo_capacity`, `cost`, `maneuverability`, `move`/`space`, `body_strength`/`hull`, `shields`, `sensors`, `weapons`...), numeric helpers (`cost_credits`, `move_value`, `move_kmh`, `space_value`, `atmosphere_value`, `atmosphere_kmh`) and the page.

sections.title: Reading a vehicle entry
sections.text:
(p.401-402)
- **Craft / Type / Scale**: manufacturer and model, classification, and scale (used by the scale rules in `combat-injuries.md#scale`).
- **Skill**: the operation skill and specialization (for example repulsorlift operation: airspeeder). Some vehicles list an **unskilled** penalty for pilots without the specialization.
- **Crew**: standard crew plus gunners; `skeleton` is the minimum crew and the penalty added to piloting difficulties. **Crew Skill**: typical die codes.
- **Passengers, Cargo Capacity**, **Cover** (Full, 3/4, 1/2, 1/4 or none; `combat-modifiers.json`), **Altitude Range** (flying vehicles), **Cost** (new).
- **Maneuverability**: dice added to the pilot's roll for movement and vehicle dodges. **Move**: meters per round at cruising speed; the all-out speed in km/h follows after the semicolon. **Body Strength**: the die code rolled to resist damage.
- **Weapons**: type and number, fire arc, crew, skill, fire control (added to the gunner's roll), range (four numbers mean point-blank/short/medium/long; closer than point-blank is Very Difficult) and damage. "Fire-linked" weapons are listed as a group.

sections.title: Reading a starship entry
sections.text: Same layout plus: **Hyperdrive Multiplier** and **Backup**, **Nav Computer**, **Consumables**, **Space** (Space units per round at cruising speed), **Atmosphere** (Move and km/h in atmosphere), **Hull** (die code to resist damage), **Shields**, and **Sensors** with four modes written `range/dice` (passive, scan, search, focus). Weapons list **Space Range** and **Atmosphere Range**. Capital ships also list their starfighter, ground or other complements under `extras`. Entries with `hull_note` or `shields_note` carry a footnote from the book (for example back-up shield dice on the MC80).

sections.title: Replacement systems and upgrades
sections.text:
(p.447-452) `ship-upgrades.json`. Meant for freighters and space transports: capital ships are rarely modified and starfighters are already at their limits. Every system has a weight subtracted from cargo capacity; costs do not include installation.
- **Drives**: replacement ion drives (Space ratings 4 to 12, 10,000 to 500,000 credits; military ones are illegal and doubly hard to modify) and a baffled stealth drive.
- **Hyperdrives**: x1 (15,000), x2 (10,000), x3 (7,000), x4 (4,000), x5 (2,500) plus the very illegal x1/2. Any hyperdrive fits a freighter with room; brand affects installation difficulty.
- **Deflector shields**: 1D (4,000 credits, 6 tons), 2D (10,000, 8), 3D (20,000, 10).
- **Weapons**: eleven sample weapons (blaster, laser and ion cannons, a turbolaser, torpedo and missile launchers) with fire control, damage, cost and weight. Weapons need a fee (about 30% of the price) and a permit; up to three identical weapons can be linked (+1D for two, +2D for three; about 100 credits per weapon).
- **Sensors and countermeasures**: sensor jammer (4,000), decoys (2,000), sensor equipment costs; no working cloaking device is known.
- **Miscellaneous**: fuel and solar converters, scoops, tractor beam (8,000 credits, 2D fire control and damage), secret compartments (200 / 400 / 1,000 credits per ton by grade), cargo jettison, passenger conversion, refrigeration, navigation computer (2,000), escape pods (1,200), environmental converters.

sections.title: Using the data
sections.text:
```
jq '.items[] | select(.scale=="Starfighter") | {name, space, hull, shields, cost_credits}' data/starships.json
jq '.items[] | select(.name=="AT-AT") | .weapons' data/vehicles.json
jq '.systems[] | {name, cost_credits, weight}' data/ship-upgrades.json
```

aquatic-vehicle-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in aquatic vehicle repair, and allows the design of various aquatic vehicles and aquatic vehicle systems.

armor-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in armor repair. Allows the design of various types of personal armor

capital-ship-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 5D in capital ship repair, 4D capital ship weapon repair, and 2D computer programming/repair. It is possible to take this skill without the required die codes in capital ship weapon repair and computer programming/repair, but the bonus effects from engineering would not apply to those areas. This skill allows the design of various capital ships, and capital ship systems.

civil-industrial-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 1D in bureaucracy, 2D business, 3D demolitions, 1D law enforcement, and 2D in any two repair skills. This is a skill that relates to the building, maintenance, and modification of settlements, civic projects, businesses, and factories.

computer-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 5D in computer programming/repair. This skill allows the design and construction of various computers, computer software, and complex computer networks.

droid-engineering-advanced.text: Requires Requires 5D in droid repair or 5D in droid programming. This skill allows the design and construction of droids, See the “Droids” chapter for rules pertaining to the use of this skill.

equipment-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 5D in equipment repair. This skill allows for the design and construction of various small equipment items and non-blaster weapons (e.g. vibroblades, breath masks, slugthrowers, comlinks).

ground-vehicle-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in ground vehicle repair. This skill allows the design of various vehicles and vehicle systems.

hover-vehicle-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in hover vehicle repair. This skill allows the design of various hover vehicles and hover vehicle systems.

installation-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 2D computer programming/repair, 2D demolitions, and 1D in any two of the following — (A) capital ship engineering, (A) civil/industrial engineering, (A) space transports engineering, (A) starfighter engineering, or (A) weapons engineering. This skill allows for the construction of fortified bases, strong holds, and other military installations.

medicine-advanced.text: Advanced skill — requires first aid of at least 5D.

repulsorlift-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in repulsorlift repair. This skill allows the design of various repulsorlift vehicles and repulsorlift vehicle systems.

space-transport-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 5D in space transports repair. This skill allows the design of various space transports and space transport systems.

starfighter-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 5D starfighter repair and 3D starship weapons repair. It is possible to take this skill without the required die code in starship weapons repair, but the bonus effects from engineering would only apply to non-weapon functions. This skill allows the design of various starfighters and starfighter systems.

submersible-vehicle-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in submersible vehicle repair. This skill allows the design of various submersible vehicles and submersible vehicle systems.

walker-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 4D in walker repair. This skill allows the design of various walkers and walker systems.

weapon-engineering-advanced.text: Requires 5D in any two of the following — blaster repair, capital ship weapon repair, demolitions, equipment repair, starship weapon repair. This skill allows for the design and construction of various weapons systems and blasters.

schema.title: Star Wars RPG (REUP) character sheet
schema.description: Structure of the two-page character sheet (book pages 501-502). Dice codes are objects so they can be added and compared; the book's text form is kept in `text`. Reference lists use the ids of the knowledge base (skills.json, species.json, force-powers.json, weapons.json, armor.json, tables/advantages-disadvantages.json).

force_attributes.description: Force skills (control, sense, alter); absent or 0D for characters without them.

wound_status.description: The sheet has boxes for Stunned (1), Wounded (2), Incapacitated (1) and Mortally Wounded (1).

armor.description: Sheet columns: Type, AV, Notes (armor value).

weapons.description: Sheet columns: Type, Damage, Range short/medium/long, and an ammo row of 18 boxes.

skills.description: Only skills that were improved or learned; an unlisted skill uses the attribute.
